scores.why: It combines the owner's two strongest signals on every page. Signal Box's line language is here throughout: the Coming up track from a lit now lamp, the To do timetable margin, the Lately added rail, the Chat thread hung from Vera's mark ending in a green ring, the ringed and bracketed page head, and the dot under the current page. The tube's real halo is back only on the live list (mind, Send, the lamps, the lit run, the monitor's bloom and spill), over grounded slate, steel-cyan and cream, and the setup tray is now slate instead of olive. It loses a little for the thick pewter monitor cases and the brown and plum tints on the Lately added cards.

This has the strongest return of the original's soul. The question is typed on a scanlined green tube that warms up from a line, and Status gets a lit moving-coil needle. Beside it is the calmest, best-typeset desk in the round: condensed heads, Plex Mono figures, WHO/DUE heads, leaders, amber 'was due' and a lit NOW rail. The line art is thinner than Track Diagram's, it has only rails, and the rounded terminal body is still a heavy case.

Light as data done beautifully: the Ideas tube plots the family's places round a lit home, and Home and Plans chart the coming weeks. The four one-meaning signals give grounded colour a job on Status. The radar's turning sweep is gone, and the map's small, crowded labels lose some of the period magic.
Same full line system as its Aglow child, and still the owner-favoured structure. The light on the live things is weaker, and the olive-bronze setup tray reads brown, which the owner has rejected.
A handsome, calm page template with a real lit tube per page and ASCII bars on To do. Its Joined child fixes the small Home box and the lost headline, so the parent now sits just behind it.

A grounded programme listing with good typesetting (figure over label, a NOW divider), rails lit from now, and a trace on the Next up glass. It is quieter in CRT character and line art than the leaders, and the wide head column still reads a bit like an admin page.

Same fine line art as Track Diagram, but setting every row in Plex Mono 600 makes the lists denser and louder. It also reads a little like a code editor, where the owner wants a calm machine beside a warm family hand.
The tubes that draw the family's weeks and dues are real CRT data-light, and the tables are well set. It has little line art, the monitor cases are thick, and Home below the fold is plain.

This is a bold, coherent new structure. A light-trail spine drops through the gutter and turns into every bank at a lit node, each section's trail is in its own muted colour, and the afterglow is the only one in the round you can actually see. The Coming up cells are lovely. It is held back by extended tracked caps on the title, nav and buttons, a page made mostly of equal outlined boxes (the owner likes boxes on items less), 22 small targets on Home, and a Tron feel that edges away from a green-screen tube.

A poetic concept: light only through cuts in a matte plate. The lead-rule section heads and the amber-marked late slot are good ideas. On screen, though, it is calm to the point of plain: underlined titles in every row, an 82% green share on Home and a bare Status, with the backlit idea hard to read outside Send and the monitor.

It varies across the page: big condensed quote heads with figures in section colours, three board cells and slate throughout. But the Signal Box lines are mostly gone, the numbered key bar is busy, and the violet 12 is off-period.
Strong tubes and a clear sommaire. It reads as a rack of boxes with brass warmth and empty stretched cells, and there is little line art.

Fraunces folios and drive-time figures are real typesetting and would please the owner's eye. But the almanac serif and the heather, rose and brass inks pull away from the CRT, and Home's cells are emptier than before.

The huge lowercase headline with a glowing 'mind' is the most striking lit word in the round, and the round radar is grand. Elsewhere it is a printed Bauhaus poster, with ochre and terracotta squares and pink wishes, colours the owner reads as off-motif.

A disciplined drafting grid with a nice title-block footer, and the tubes are lit. The blueprint dilutes the green-screen motif into a room's colour, capitals are everywhere, and the family's lines are violet revision clouds, a colour the owner calls off-period.
The single-quote typography is a good device. The plum cast (which the owner dislikes), the second ALT bar and the many small targets outweigh it.
The scope that pulses the plans and the LED countdown meters are gorgeous period phosphor. The walnut, brass and manila cabinet is exactly the brown that the owner said does not work with the CRT.
Yardstick. It has the soul (glow, bloom, lit dots), but it is too bright, too contrasty and nearly monochrome, and it lacks the grounded colour and structure the owner has since asked for.

fixes.suggestion:
Keep the line system and the light list whole.
- Monitor cases: thin the pewter slabs to a 2-3px graphite bezel with fine detail (a hairline inner lip, the vent ticks, the lamp). The owner has asked for this since round 7.
- Lately added cards: drop the brown, plum and teal fills. Put the kind colour in the ring lamp only.
- To do: carry the lit run down the vertical track to the now lamp, as on Coming up.
- Afterglow: make it visible, with a 10-14% steel wash and a sage edge fading over about 1s.
- Ideas: graft Desk Terminal, Mapped's plotted map onto the Ideas tube so the light draws data.
- Borrow Desk Terminal's WHO/DUE column heads and amber 'was due' words for the To do page.

Keep the map and the four signals.
- Bring back a slow sweep beam over the map (without crossing text), so the period motion survives.
- Split the three downtown places with a small offset and a leader.
- Make the map's dots links.
- Give 'off' a shape distinct from the numbered band rings.

Keep:
- the spine with lit nodes and the section-coloured trails, which the owner values as lines that delimit and lead the eye;
- the visible afterglow;
- the Coming up cells with their large date;
- the thin-cased monitor with its own floor.
Fix:
- Set the title in a condensed face at about 2.5rem, not extended light caps.
- Put the nav, buttons and links in sentence case.
- Replace equal outlined cells with one-line rows for To do, Status and Lately added, since the boxes are dense.
- Fix the 22 small targets.
- Keep the perspective floor to the foot only.

Graft the scope drawing the next four weeks as pulses, and the LED countdown meters, onto the leader's slate and graphite. Drop the walnut, brass, manila and brass holders entirely. Brass becomes steel, and the drawer labels become the leader's plain heads.

Keep the huge glowing 'what's on your mind?' as Home's one poster moment, and keep the round radar. Replace the ochre and terracotta squares and pink wishes with steel and slate, and let the rest of the page be the leader's structure.

The idea is worth keeping: light only where the plate is cut, with the lead-rule heads and the late slot. Stop underlining every row title, restore a clear step between heads and rows, and give Status one lit instrument so the plate is not plain.

judges.notes:
I read this through the owner's first-hand reactions: grounded, supporting colour (cyan and steel in measure; no brown, pink or heavy violet), Signal Box's line art carried through every page, and the lit CRT glow brought back where the phosphor is. Track Diagram Aglow is the only entrant that does both of the owner's strongest wishes on every page: the lines that delimit and lead the eye, and the halo back on the live list. So it leads for this lens, even though its change from its parent is small. Desk Terminal, Joined is a close second: it has the most CRT soul (the question typed on the glass, the needle meter) and the best typesetting, but less line art.

The breed this lens asks for is Track Diagram's lines and relit lamps, set on Desk Terminal's typographic desk, with a tube that draws data (Mapped's map, the needle, Signal Catalogue's scope pulses) in a thin, detailed case.

Among the wild entrants, Grid Console's spine and its visible afterglow are the new ideas most in the owner's taste. Signal Catalogue and Dessau have the best lit graphics but are held back by warm, brown and printed-ink grounds the owner has rejected. Every leader still has the thick pewter or graphite monitor case the owner flagged in round 7.

scores.why: The source of the soul: every lit thing has its full halo, the greeting glows from below and the tubes bloom. But glow is not scarce, because green runs through every icon, link and button, so the page glares rather than lights up. That is the Matrix the family named.

The truest return of the tube this round. Home's terminal reads as one machine: scrollback, then the question typed at display size in blooming VT323 under a block cursor, then the box as the glass's last rows, and it warms up from a bright line. The Status moving-coil meter (hot needle, hatched overrun, ghost average) is the most period-true lit instrument on any page. NOW lamps and a lit NOW tick carry the light into the desk, and the desk stays matte.

The best explanation yet of why the glow is scarce: light shows only where the plate is cut. Next up's window blooms and spills onto its bevel, the bar has an underglow, lamps are pinholes, and Vera's newest line glows at the edge. The slot traces (Coming up, Plans, To do with amber late ticks) are light drawing data. It loses points because 'mind', stencilled as it is, barely blooms at 100%, and the greeting lost its lit pool from below.

Still a real terminal on every page, with the question on the glass, ASCII late bars, the spend tube and glowing lamps. Its own child now does it better: here Home's box is a loose form under the tube, and the Status tube is a plain readout, not an instrument.

The greeting keeps its lit glass pool, Next up's pulse trace works as data, and rails lit from a breathing NOW lamp run through Coming up, To do and Status. It is calm and alive, but thinner in light than the terminals, and below the fold it is mostly a matte listing.

The Ideas map is a beautiful new lit picture: home glowing at the centre, and numbered places at their true bearing and drive. The four signals give each lamp a meaning. But Home lost the radar's sweep and its afterglow, the most loved tube gesture, and the hours chart reads as a plotted spreadsheet more than a scope.

This does exactly what the soul asked. 'mind' has its two-layer halo again, Send pools light, the box blooms, and the run of track from NOW is visibly lit, so side by side at 1.5x it is warmer than its parent. The change is small, though, and the page afterglow under the bar has dropped below visibility.

A lit display question ('mind' glowing at 64px), the greeting's glass pool, the mark's cursor, numbered function keys and a Status lamp row (ANSWERS/KEYS/LINKS lit dots) make a live terminal desk on calm slate. Below the greeting, though, the big figures are in section colours rather than light, and Chat's quoted last line is in bone, so the phosphor thins out.

You type on the glass: the question and the prompt are on Home's tube, and Chat's box is a lit '> Message Vera' line. Every page has its own green summary screen. The brass warmth and pixel pictograms pull it toward a kiosk.

The tubes draw the family's own weeks, due dates, spend and places, with full bloom, scanlines and sweep, and the tables around them stay matte. The sweep still crosses Next up's text, and the resting traces are low.
The best 'lit where live' line (the lamp and the lit track from it) on steel and slate. At 100% the halos are thinner than its Aglow child's, and 'mind' and Send barely glow.

It keeps every tube, the question typed on glass and Chat's lit prompt. But the loudest shapes on each page are now large Fraunces folios and figures in printed ink ('300', '900', '2h45'), so the personality has moved from videotex screen to printed almanac, with the light as a guest.

Home's greeting is the most alive of the round. 'mind' is huge, with scanlines running through the lit letters and a real halo, and a big round radar scope blooms off the edge with its sweep and blips. Every page gets one round phosphor screen holding its live figure. Below the fold, though, it is a matte Bauhaus poster (solid ink squares, thick colour bars, lowercase Outfit), so the green screen is a guest in someone else's print.

Real terminal behaviour: a command path with a cursor, an LED on the current key, a Status lamp row and tubes at full bloom. The plum-graphite housing still reads off-period, and its slate child now does it better.

The same light as its parent, and the VT323 set to the cell pitch with a double-height headline is a true terminal touch on the glass. But Plex Mono across every row and form spreads the machine's voice everywhere, so the tube's voice is no longer scarce, and the page reads like a code editor rather than a desk lit by one screen.

The scope drawing one heartbeat pulse per plan, with glowing peaks, is a genuinely lit, period-feeling instrument. So are the LED countdown bars and Vera as a waveform. But walnut, brass label holders and typewriter titles put the green screen in a 1930s card cabinet on a brown ground. It is a steampunk library with a scope in it, not a green screen.

The tubes are kept whole, 'mind' and Send glow, and the spine's lit nodes are a nice lit structure. But the Tron perspective floor, the teal light-trails and the all-caps titles are a different sci-fi. They make the page a vector-game set, and teal line work competes with the phosphor as the page's light.

The tubes still bloom, and the idea of keeping the phosphor only where the machine is is right. But a drafting grid printed across every page, violet revision clouds and capital lettering make each page an architectural drawing that has a monitor on it. The grid texture washes the whole screen and the page is no longer lit.

fixes.suggestion: Keep everything on the glass: the typed question, the box as the tube's last rows, the warm-up line and the moving-coil meter. Fixes: (1) VT323's tall-tick apostrophe shows at 30px in 'What's'; substitute a straight glyph or kern it. (2) The row afterglow on the desk is invisible in the stills (4th round running), so either give it a real 0.12s-on/1.2s-fade lit edge you can see or drop it. (3) Let the terminal spill a faint 60-80px green pool onto the desk beside it, as the original tube lit the desk under Send, so machine and desk feel like one room. (4) Rest the meter's ghost needle on the day's peak or the limit so a $0.00 still reads. (5) Trim Chat's repeated Vera (bar, head row, terminal, every line).

Keep the rule that light only shows through a cut: it is the clearest law for scarcity yet, and it holds on every page. The slot traces with amber late ticks are the round's best light-as-data. Fixes: (1) 'mind' is stencilled but barely blooms. Light coming through a stencil should show the full E1 two-layer halo at 100%, and a thin light-leak below the letters would give back the greeting's lit pool. (2) Put Status's 30-day spend in a slot too, so Status has a trace as well as the $0.00 window. (3) Underlining every row title makes the plate read busy and admin; underline on hover only. (4) The phosphor's bevel spill is lovely on Next up. Give the Ideas round window and the idea page's own blip window the same spill.

Keep (1) the display question with scanlines running through the lit word, (2) the big blooming radar scope on Home, and (3) one round phosphor screen per page holding that page's live figure: that is a system. Fixes: (1) The round screen should say what the page doesn't, so '2 LATE' on To do rather than repeating '4 to do'. (2) Below the fold the Bauhaus inks take over. Thin the colour bars to 2px caps and turn the solid kind squares into outlined marks, so the page is calm and the round screens stay the only light. (3) Carry one lit element into the rows below (a NOW lamp on Coming up) so the light doesn't end at the greeting. (4) Seat the Next up monitor clear of the radar rather than overlapping it.

Keep the scope (one glowing pulse per plan, with peaks that flare) and the LED countdown bars: they are the round's most musical lit instrument, worth grafting onto a terminal's glass. Fixes: replace walnut and brass with graphite and slate (a brown ground turns green-on-black into green-on-brown, as the r7-r11 cases showed), drop the riveted brass title holders for plain condensed heads, and set titles in sans, not typewriter mono. Keep brass, if at all, only for call numbers.

Graft the Ideas map (home lit at the centre, numbered places at their true bearing and drive) into the leader, and make its blips links. On Home, keep a sweep: draw the coming weeks as a scope trace with a moving beam and wake, not an hours-by-days dot plot, which reads as a spreadsheet.

The right direction, too small to see at half size. Let the lit run of track carry a travelling afterglow wake from the NOW lamp toward the next stop, and restore the greeting's lit pool from below at the original's strength. Those two would make the relight visible at page scale.

Keep the keyed title block and the strict 24px rhythm. They are good typesetting. Take the drafting grid off the page ground (keep it only as margin ticks, or inside the tubes as a graticule), drop the violet revision clouds for the family's bubbles, and use sentence case, so the page is dark and quiet again and the tube is the only light on the sheet.

Keep the spine with lit square nodes where a bank starts. Make the nodes phosphor only where the bank holds something live (late, now), drop the perspective floor and the teal trails, and use sentence-case titles. The structure then reads as a lit wiring diagram of the page rather than a Tron set.

judges.notes: Soul, round 13: the two informed entrants brought back the most of the original's light, and each made it mean something. Desk Terminal, Joined types on the tube, holds the box as the glass's last rows, warms up from a bright line and puts a real moving-coil meter on Status. Backlit Plate gives every glow a physical cause (a cut in a matte plate) and draws the family's weeks as lit slot traces. Both keep the rest of the page grounded and change Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas, Status, Plans and To do, so both pass the owner's 'not a wash in the corner' test. The mutants that only relit (Aglow) are visibly better at 1.5x, but too small a step to see at page scale. The wild entrants all kept the tube and its full kit, but most made it a guest in another world: a blueprint, a walnut card cabinet, a Bauhaus poster, the Tron grid. The soul lens wants the green screen as the host, with other materials serving it, not the reverse. The best single moments of light this round came from the wild lane, though: Dessau's scanlined display 'mind' and big blooming scope, Signal Catalogue's pulse trace, and Mapped's Ideas map. They are worth grafting onto the terminal leader. There are two recurring holes: row afterglow is still invisible in stills (fourth round), and the greeting's lit pool from below was dropped by Backlit Plate and both terminals. Today scores 6.0 through this lens and the best 8.8, so the leaders now carry more of the original's soul than the original does, because their light is scarce and does a job.

scores.why: A clear but one-note identity: green on black everywhere, stock dark-mode cards below the fold. It is the Matrix look the family named, with no companions and no typographic voice.

The freshest and most joyful identity of the round. Every page is a poster: a big lowercase Outfit name, a square of print ink, and a round phosphor tube holding the page's one live figure. Four shapes have four jobs, and the footer even carries their legend. Below the fold on Home, the ink bars over each column and the kinds as filled print squares are grounded colour a family would call lovely. It weakens on To do and Status, which fall back to stock cards and pills under the poster.

The most inventive complete system, and a witty pun on 'plans'. It has a drafting grid with grid references, a title block on every sheet (and one at the foot as the footer), dimension lines ('IN 2 DAYS' between ticks), hatched swatches for the kinds, and the family's chat lines drawn as violet revision clouds. The CRT becomes a component drawn on the sheet with the full kit. It is held back by flat one-size lettering, heavy capitals and a grid that sits under every reading area.

The switchboard typeset as an almanac. Light Fraunces figures in each section's ink (a 300 folio, '≈ 2h45 ← MIN' drive times, month days set large) make typography the picture, which suits an owner who loves typesetting. Plans is a beautiful page. The equal cells leave dead darkspace (Restaurants, Memory, the idea cards), and four faces is a lot.

The best-made typographic device in the carried lines: condensed titles followed by the section's figure in its colour and a stacked mono change line. It is laid on Evening's calm slate, and the three board cells, the Ideas register and the To do register are refined and exact. It is less surprising as an identity, Status is still monochrome, and the footer's shortcut legend is clutter.

Desk Terminal made more whole. The headline is typed on the glass with the box as the tube's last rows, a moving-coil spend meter sits on Status, and a lit NOW tick runs in To do. It is handsome and systematic, but the desk beside it is still a fairly conventional slate-and-steel dashboard, and VT323's apostrophe gaps in 'What ' s'.

The plotted map on the Ideas tube (home lit at the centre, numbered dots by bearing and drive) is a genuinely period-true graphic with a job. Home's hours chart is harder to read, and outside the tube it is the parent unchanged.
A strong, memorable device: one cased terminal beside a matte desk. The desk itself is calm but generic slate rows with steel, so the style lives mostly in the left column.

The videotex sommaire is a distinctive, confident structure: page numbers, a rack of cells, a green screen under each plate. The pixel pictograms and empty cells read a little like a costume beside its Folio descendant.

A sophisticated programme listing: margin figures, rails lit from now, a trace on Next up. It is tasteful and grounded, but the Home hero is crowded and the page reads as a refined admin listing more than a memorable mood.

A warm walnut-and-brass card catalogue with typed index cards, Dewey call numbers ('790.1 OAK 01'), rod holes and LED countdown meters. It is the most material and grounded palette on the board. The ECG-style pulse on Next up reads as a hospital monitor, the squiggle ornaments and brass label holders tip into costume, and typewriter titles on every card are heavy.

Coherent and calm, with outlined cells, a light-trail spine lit at section-coloured nodes and hatched blank plates. But it borrows Tron's Grid wholesale (the perspective floor, the wide-tracked caps), so the identity feels borrowed rather than FamilyDB's own, and outlines everywhere make it busy.
Bold quote typography and a command-path feel, still on a plum cast. Its best ideas have been better realised in Quote Board at Evening.
Tubes that draw the family's data (a due-date scope on To do, a spend scope on Status) are lovely period objects. Everything else is plain tables that could belong to any dark dashboard.
A signal-box track diagram with lamps is a distinctive rule that runs through Home, Chat, To do and Status. The rounded slate cards around it are stock.

At page scale it is indistinguishable from Track Diagram Relit. The added glow on the mark, 'mind', Send and the lamps is tasteful but is exactly the 'few small lit things' change the owner says looks identical.

A beautiful idea in words: a matte plate cut only where the machine is live. In the shots it reads as a plain dark page with narrow heads and leading rules. The traces on Coming up, Plans and To do are the only new character, and the steel and denim companions are timid.
Setting the family's rows in Plex Mono turns a warm diagram into a code editor. The rows are denser and louder, and the typesetting loses warmth rather than gaining hierarchy.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the posters, the round phosphor tube carrying one live figure, the squares of ink, the column ink bars, the kinds as filled print squares and the footer's shape legend. Carry the system below the poster, where To do and Status revert to stock cards, pills and a generic filter box. Set To do as rows, with a square tick, an amber triangle for late and a circle lamp for a reminder. Make To do's round screen show the late count instead of repeating the open count. Give Status's cards the 01/02/03 numerals as a left margin, not an inline prefix. Step the Home headline down a notch (about 88px, tighter tracking) so 'mind' glows without the black lowercase shouting. Shift the card surface from navy (#13171e) toward neutral graphite so bone ink and ink squares sit on print, not blue. Close the empty band beside Plans' name by moving its round screen in or giving it a lede. Fix the 31 small Home targets.

Keep the title block (sheet, note, number) on each page and at the foot, the grid references, the dimension-line counts, the hatched kind swatches, the CRT drawn as a dashed-outline component, and above all the violet revision clouds for the family's lines. Fix the hierarchy with a second lettering step: the drawing title larger (about 1.25x), notes and data in sentence case, capitals only for block labels and keys. Let the drafting grid fade under reading areas (tables, chat, forms), leaving it strong only in the margins and gutters so the sheet stays calm. Let a To do row without notes take one grid line, not two, and mark late on To do. Give the phone frame a hairline edge so the grid does not stop abruptly.

Keep the light Fraunces figures in each section's ink: the folios, drive times, month days and initials. Plans is the best-typeset page on the board. Fill the dead cells: Restaurants should print its count and the two names, and Memory a count or the latest remembered line; alternatively let those cells span half height. Shorten the idea cards so the figure sits beside 'for X' rather than beneath a well of darkspace. Pare back to three faces (Fraunces, Plex Sans, VT323) by using Plex Sans small caps for labels instead of Plex Mono. Pass `late` so overdue leaves print in ochre.

Keep the quote heads (condensed title, figure in the section colour, stacked mono unit and change line), the board cells, and the Ideas and To do registers. Give Status some colour beyond steel: the lamp strip's figures in their owners' inks and an amber figure for 'needs a look'. Move the footer's access-key legend into a small help popover. Cap Vera's large last line in Chat at about 1.25rem, and only for short replies, so a long answer never becomes a headline. Let To do's empty tray on Home collapse to its content.

Keep the walnut-and-brass palette, the typed index cards with call numbers and rod holes, and the LED countdown meters, which are the round's most grounded, material colour. Replace the ECG trace with a scope that cannot read as a heartbeat (square pulses, or a bar per plan with afterglow). Drop the squiggle ornaments between drawer labels. Set only card heads in the typewriter face and keep rows and meta in the sans. Lose the brass holder on page titles in favour of a plain brass label rule.

Keep the section-coloured spine nodes, the equal cells and the hatched blank plates. Drop the perspective floor except on sign-in and 404, and swap the thin wide-tracked title caps for a face of its own, so it stops reading as borrowed Tron. Lighten the outline weight on inner cells so the lattice recedes.

The plate idea needs to show. Give the plate a visible edge and bevel, and let the cuts be seen as cuts, with light spilling onto a bevel lip, not a glowing border. Give the steel companion a second, warmer job so the page is not 82% green.

judges.notes: Through the creativity-and-style lens this round is the first where the wild entrants beat the carried leaders on identity. Dessau, Blueprint and Folio each change the whole page (Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas, Status, Plans) with an idea-led system, while keeping the full phosphor kit inside the machine: the round tubes, the drawn CRT component and the green sommaire tube. That is exactly the owner's 'bright green where it needs to be, grounded elsewhere'. Meanwhile the carried Desk Terminal, Evening Listing and Track Diagram lines are converging on one look, slate trays with steel reverse video and denim links. That look is refined and calm but increasingly generic as a style. The mutants of Track Diagram (Aglow, Monospaced) are near-duplicates at page scale; Monospaced shows that setting data in mono makes the page colder, not better typeset. Typography was the round's strongest lever: Quote Board's figure-after-title heads, Folio's Fraunces figures and Dessau's poster names are three distinct type systems worth grafting. A crossover to try next round is Dessau's round tube and shape legend with Quote Board's head figures and registers below the fold, or Folio's figures inside Blueprint's title blocks. Every one of the top wilds still needs its system carried through To do and Status, where each falls back to stock cards. Today's page scores 4.3 here; the best is 8.2.

scores.why: Yardstick. Rounded cards float on bare black, glow is spread over everything, and filters are selects beside lists. There is no written type scale and no shared row drawing, so each page is its own layout.

The most complete template. Every page names itself in one head row with its primary action, the terminal fits or sticks, and each page's controls sit in the terminal as latched keys. The question and box are built into the tube's last rows over a keyboard ledge, and the Status needle meter is lit data. Held back by a ~290px dead void under the Home terminal at 1280, a VT323 question with a floating apostrophe, and red 'no key' rings that read as warnings.

The most elegant new system. It uses one square slate plate, a small vocabulary of cuts (a slot for time, a round window for place, a 4:3 window for the screen), rule-led condensed heads with the count on the same line, and one-line rows with tabular facts. Home has a real 40px question with the glowing 'mind', and the lit slots on Home, Plans and To do are data. Weak points: Settings and Family are only restyled, and still carry rounded tiles. Every row title is underlined. The 4:3 windows have spare glass. The open select list draws as an empty black band.

A real system gain on the Desk Terminal: every lamp is one of four signals with one meaning each, and 'off' is a pewter ring, so a gap no longer reads as an alarm. The Ideas map draws the family's places as light. The Home WHEN chart is less legible than the radar it replaced, and Home grows about 100px.

Still a sound page template: machine and desk apart, one mechanism for every filter, a Contents plate and a status foot. Its children fix its known faults (a small Home box, a small VT323 question), so it now reads as the base rather than the best.

Best display type system this round. Each head is a condensed title with the section's figure and a stacked unit and change line, the Home board is compact, there are 0 small targets now (53 in its parent), and it has the only row afterglow that clearly registers. It loses on digits beside every bar key plus a shortcut legend in the footer (noise), setup folded to one visible step, board figures set far from their labels, amber doing two jobs (the To do section and caution), and Vera's last chat line set large.

A disciplined listing system (a head column with a figure over a label, column heads, a NOW divider, 2 late as a link) that holds on every page. It is a known quantity now: the lit rails and trace are small beside the new templates.

Moving setup onto slate fixes the olive tray, and the lit runs are correct. At page scale it is nearly indistinguishable from its parent, and the parent's selects-beside-lists and card grid on Ideas remain.
The column-headed tables and data tubes are sound, but Home and To do keep today's form-then-list structure, with a Show select and a Filter button. Its good parts now live better in the leaders.
The sommaire rack is the best 'where is everything' device, but half-empty equal cells, tracked-caps buttons and card-grid Ideas and To do keep it from being a system for daily reading.
Lines carry order with restraint, but the filters are still selects in a boxed form, Ideas is a card grid, and the Status items are boxes inside boxes. It is the page from two rounds ago.

A bold, current, genuinely systematic poster language. Four shapes have four jobs, with a legend, and each page has a poster head, a round phosphor screen and a page bar, which works on any page. It falls short in four ways. 31 small targets. The heavy 96px cream headline is now the brightest mass. The round screens hold little (To do's '4' repeats the list). Below the poster, the Ideas, To do and Settings bodies are essentially today's cards.

A real typographic statement: facts printed large in the owner's hue, and an almanac month in large numerals. But the 96px folios compete with titles, the idea cards are mostly empty darkspace around one figure, the keys are caps, and the rack still has half-empty cells.

The most rigorous grid: every block a whole number of 24px cells, and a well-set timetable for Coming up and To do. Its costume costs it: a sheet title block on every page, violet revision clouds for the family's lines, tracked caps on the nav, buttons and heads, a 15px caps question with no hierarchy, grid lines over the whole page, and 17 small targets.

'Data in mono, speech in sans' is a clear rule, but applied to every row name and title it makes lists louder and wider, wraps labels, and reads as a code editor. Mono belongs on figures and dates only.

The spine and section-coloured bank trails give order. But outlined cells for everything (To do as four cells rather than scannable rows), hatched blank plates, a perspective floor, extended caps titles and buttons, 22 small targets and an 1850px Home make it busy rather than calm.
The quote-head idea is superseded by its evening crossover. This version still has 53 small Home targets, a plum-graphite cast, a second ALT key row and one-sided chat.

The LED countdown meters and the scope pulses are good data. But a walnut-brown cast over every surface, typewriter titles, brass plaques on every page head and fake call numbers are costume, and the pulses read as an ECG.

fixes.suggestion: Fill Home's left void: put the numbered Contents plate back under the deck on Home, or make the terminal position:sticky with max-height calc(100vh - bar) so the desk runs beside it with no dead black. Take Mapped's four signals, with pewter 'off' rings instead of red for 'no key' and 'not configured'. Set the glass question with a straight apostrophe or in VT323 at the cell size, not double height. Save head-row height by putting the lede on the title's line at 1280. Keep the meter, but add the ghost peak or limit tick so $0.00 still reads.

Carry the plate grammar to Settings, Family, Memory and Wishes: square engraved keys, rule-led heads, no rounded icon tiles. Size the 4:3 windows to their words, or give Next up a fortnight trace in its spare glass. Underline row titles at about 35% ink with a 3px offset, full on hover, so rows stay links without the stripes. Fix the open select picker (it captures as an empty black band). Take amber off the third setup step unless it means 'next'. Add the terminal-style status foot (Ready, model, limit) to the READY chip on every page.

Graft the four-signal rule (on, waiting, off, needs a look) and pewter 'off' into the leader. Keep the Ideas map, but make its dots links, pass the bearing with each row, and set ring labels at 18px or more with the three downtown places spread. Return the Home glass to the radar, or label the WHEN chart with plan numbers, and use the hour chart on Plans only.

Keep the quote head (title, figure in the section colour, stacked unit and change line), the slate trays, the one bar and the visible afterglow. Drop the digits from the bar keys and the footer legend: show access keys on focus or in the menu. Show all three setup steps as a compact one-line list. Set each board figure on the label's baseline beside it. Give To do a hue other than caution amber. Set Vera's last chat line at body size.

Keep the poster head, the round screen and the four-shape legend: it is a real rule. Carry it into the bodies as one-line rows marked with the square and triangle, rather than today's cards. Put a figure the page does not already print on each round screen (late count on To do, next plan on Plans). Bring the 31 small targets up to 44px. Set nav and page names in sentence case. Drop the headline to 600 weight or bone at about 88% so the cream stops being the brightest mass.

Keep the baseline-grid discipline and the timetable rows with FROM NOW ticks. Drop the sheet title blocks, revision clouds and tracked caps on controls. Give the question and page titles their own 32-40px step, and draw the grid only inside trays at about 3%.

Keep the facts printed large, but in a right-aligned facts column on one-line rows rather than alone in empty cards. Shrink the folios to about 48px and quieter. Use sentence-case keys and grid-auto-rows:min-content so the Memory and Restaurants cells stop standing empty.

Keep the section-coloured bank trails and the corner marks. Draw To do, Coming up and Status as one-line rows, not outlined cells. Remove the hatched blanks and the perspective floor, and set heads and keys in sentence case.

judges.notes:
Through a system lens, this round's best advance is that the template, not the palette, now carries the Phosphor Interface. Desk Terminal, Joined and Backlit Plate each give every page one head, one place for its controls (latched keys), one row drawing (a one-line row with leaders and tabular facts) and one lit instrument that draws that page's data. Both bring the original light back where it belongs: glass bloom and scanlines, the Send pool, 'mind', lamps and warm-up. The rest of the page stays matte.

Principles worth writing into the standard:
(1) Mapped's four signals: on is a lit lamp, waiting a steel dot, off a pewter ring, and needs-a-look an amber bar, with red only once something has stopped. Every candidate that still draws 'no key' as a red ring shows a warning where there is none.
(2) Backlit Plate's cut grammar: the shape of a lit window says what it shows (a slot for time, a round window for place, 4:3 for the screen).
(3) Quote Board's head: a title, then the page's figure in its section colour, then a stacked unit and change line, which is the owner's typesetting at its best.

Recurring faults that still cost the new entrants: tracked or extended caps on nav, buttons and heads (Blueprint, Grid Console, Signal Catalogue, Folio), 17-31 small targets on the wilds, warm ground casts (walnut), and data drawn only in the page head while the bodies stay as today's card grids (Dessau). Only Quote Board's row afterglow registers in the capture. The leaders' hover afterglow is still invisible, for the fifth round.

On the owner's test ('reflect more of the page content'): every entrant above 7.5 changes Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas and Status. The Track Diagram mutants (Aglow, Monospaced) are the ones that still read as nearly identical to their parent.

scores.why: The yardstick. The lit greeting gives a clear first action, but 44 of 56 Home targets are under 44px. On Ideas the radar pushes every idea below the fold. To do repeats 'Edit, complete, or snooze' on every card and never says late.

Last round asked for a head row, and this is it: every inner page reads title, then the one green primary (Add an idea, Add something to do), then the terminal and the desk, with 0 small targets. Home's box now sits inside the tube under the question, which joins the glance and the action. Status adds a needle with its figure in words, To do has a lit NOW tick and amber late words, and Chat's conversation rail shows its state.

The clearest single-column sight lines on the panel: title, then the instrument, then one bank of latched keys, then the list. The same controls appear on every page: the kind keys, a one-line 'For anyone · Any but dropped' summary, a '2 late' link on the To do slot, WHO/DUE heads and a NOW divider. The squint holds and there are 0 small targets. Two costs: To do's Add sits at the foot, and every row title is underlined.

The fastest glance of the round. The title carries its figure ('Things to do 4 / 2 LATE', 'Status 6 working / 7 off'), the Filter chip states the whole filter in one line, setup shrinks to one line naming its first step, and the bar's numbered keys help keyboard users. It has 0 small targets. The shortcut legend in the footer and the Settings key losing its word add noise.

The Ideas map is the best comprehension device here: each dot carries the list's own number at its real bearing and drive. Status's four signals are coded by shape (dot, ring, bar, lamp) and come with a legend, so state no longer rests on colour alone. Home's hours-of-day chart is harder to read than the radar it replaces, and the box still sits small and low.

Still a strong working template: latched filter keys with LEDs, a status foot, the Contents plate, the To do bars on the glass and 0 small targets. Joined and Mapped now fix its costs, which are no head row before the tube, a small Home box, and title-first lost on inner pages.

Legible listing rows, a figure in every head column, WHO/DUE heads, a NOW divider, '2 late' as a link and 0 small targets. Home is long and the box sits mid-hero, and the checkbox after NOW on To do is offset from its row.
Tables with column heads scan quickly and the tube draws time. Status's narrow tables wrap each row to three or four lines, and Ideas still keeps both tabs and a Kind select.

Works the same as its parent: the Coming up track, and To do's timetable with '2 days ago' and 'yesterday' in amber beside the lamps. The light on Send and the lamps helps the eye find the action, but four bar places are still icons only.
The ordered lines help, on the Coming up track and the To do timetable. Memory, Family, Status and Settings are icons only in the bar, and one target is under 44px on every page.

The Home sommaire is still a strong 'where is everything', but it has no page names in the bar on Home, cells of equal weight lose priority in the squint, and there are tracked-caps controls and 8 to 20 small targets a page.

The large facts are glanceable (counts, due days, drive times). But Home drops the page names from the bar and sets the typed field in green VT323 on the glass. Restaurants and Memory are empty cells, To do puts Add and Show below the fold under four cards, and there are 7 to 20 small targets.

The same interaction as Track Diagram. Row names, setup sentences and the nav in Plex Mono are slower to read, the From select and 'Send where I am' shrink to 12.8px, and a target under 24px now shows on every page.
Its title-to-figure device is excellent, and Quote Board now carries it better. It still has 53 of 59 small targets on Home, a second access-key row and no late on To do.

Good table heads (DATE/PLAN/FROM NOW, DONE/TASK/WHO,WHEN), a 'DO' label beside the one primary, late in amber words and a 16px minimum font. But Home has no headline step (the question is a small caps label), the nav is all caps, sheet numbers like FD-02 and the grid's margin letters are noise, and 17 Home targets are small.

Coming up as big date cells reads at a glance, and the spine links each head to its bank. But To do becomes four cards with ISO dates ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56') and no late, Show is still a select beside the search, the titles and nav are wide caps, and 22 Home targets are small.

The LED countdown meters under each plan are a lovely glance device. But item names in Plex Mono, call numbers ('790.1 OAK 01'), a brass title plate that reads as a label, riveted caps nav, To do in cards with no late, and 8 to 15 small targets all slow the family down.

Poster titles give the strongest title-first sight line, and the shape legend in the footer is a real comprehension aid. But a 110px Home question pushes setup below the fold, four bar places are icons only, To do is cards with ISO dates and no late, and 31 Home targets are small.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the head row (title, then the one green primary) and the box on the tube's last rows. On Home the left column goes empty from about 730px down beside Setup, Coming up and To do, so make the terminal sticky there or let Lately added rise into it. The 40px VT323 'What's' shows its tall-tick apostrophe, so use a curly apostrophe or keep VT323 to the cursor. On the phone the bezel puts about 100px between the field and Send, so put Send in the tube's last row or directly under the field. Give Plans a primary ('Add a plan') in its head row. Say '4 more after Next up' to end the off-by-one. Graft in Mapped's Ideas map and its four-signal legend on Status.

Keep the one-bank latched keys, the filter summary chip, the lit slot trace with its '2 late' link, and the cut-shape semantics (slot is time, round is place). Move 'Add something to do' up into the head as To do's green primary, as Ideas already does. Underline row titles only on hover and focus, with the dotted leader carrying the row. Fold the per-page READY chip into one status foot that links to Status. Make the Home Coming up trace's NOW and date labels larger than VT323 at about 14px.

Keep the title figure, the one-line Filter chip, the setup line naming only its first step, and the NOW divider with full late dates. Move the shortcut legend out of the footer into a '?' key or the Settings page. Drop the bar's number badges to a quieter value, and give Settings its word back at 1280px. Use a red ring, not a grey dot, for a missing fallback, so a real gap does not look like a key left off on purpose. Stop the To do cell's empty tray with grid-auto-rows:min-content.

Keep the Ideas map, and make each numbered dot a link to its row (a 44px hit area, not aria-hidden). Keep the shape-coded four signals with their legend and write them into the standard. Replace Home's hours-of-day chart, whose axis a family has to decode, with Joined's lit trace plus the box on the glass, or label its axes in words.

Keep the lowercase poster title with its square and the round live figure, and the shape legend. Set Home's question at about 64px so the box and setup rise above the fold. Put words back on Memory, Family, Status and Settings. Replace To do's cards with ISO dates by one-line rows with worded dates and amber late. Bring every target to 44px.

Keep the column-headed tables and the 'DO' label beside the one primary: they are clear. Drop the sheet numbers (FD-02) and the grid's margin letters and numbers. Set the nav and controls in sentence case. Give Home a real headline step (the question at 32-40px, not a caps label in the box). Bring the 17 small Home targets to 44px.

Keep the LED countdown meters and the plan scope, and graft them into the leader's Coming up. Set item names in the sans, not Plex Mono, and drop the call numbers. Make page titles type rather than a brass plate. Show late in amber words on To do, as one-line rows instead of 2-up cards. Set the nav in sentence case, without rivets.

Give Home the bar's page names back. Set the typed words in the sans on a glass-tinted field, not green VT323. Span or fill the empty Restaurants and Memory cells. On To do, put Add and Show above the task cells and set late in amber. Take tracked caps off the controls ('ADD AN IDEA').

judges.notes: Through this lens the round's clear advance is that the two informed entrants answered last round's interaction faults directly. Desk Terminal, Joined puts a head row first on every inner page, so the sight line is title, then the one green primary, then content. It keeps the terminal's latched keys and status foot, moves the Home box onto the tube so the glance and the action are one place, and has 0 small targets on all 13 pages. Backlit Plate gets the same order in a single column: title, instrument, one bank of latched keys, list. Its one-line filter summary chip and the '2 late' link on the To do slot are the most readable state controls of the round. Quote Board at Evening has the fastest glance: a figure beside every title, a filter chip that states the whole filter, and setup shrunk to one line naming its next step. Desk Terminal, Mapped's Ideas map (dots numbered as the list, at the real bearing and drive) and its shape-coded signals with a legend are the best new comprehension devices. Both should be grafted into the leader. The four wild entrants each bring one good device: Blueprint's column-headed tables and 'DO' label, Signal Catalogue's LED countdown meters, Dessau's poster title and shape legend, and Grid Console's date cells. All four fail the same way as last round's wilds: 8 to 31 small Home targets, caps nav, and To do as cards with no late (ISO dates on two of them). All four entrants that renamed the nav in caps or icons lost comprehension. What this lens would write into the standard: (a) every page opens on a head row (title, its figure, the one primary); (b) each page has one bank of latched keys and a one-line chip stating the filter; (c) late is amber words plus a count link, split from upcoming by a NOW divider; (d) state is coded by shape as well as colour, with a legend where lamps carry meaning; (e) the lit instrument draws the page's own data and its marks point to the rows by number.

scores.why: Yardstick. One humanist sans at timid steps: small titles beside big tiles, card grids that spread type at the same size everywhere, dates set as raw '2026-09-27 19:56', no column heads and no tabular alignment. The only typographic character is VT323 on the glass.

This is the most confident type system of the round, and it runs on every page. Each head is a condensed title with the page's figure in its colour and a stacked mono legend ('Ideas 12 IN ALL / LAST ADDED SUN 27 SEP', 'Things to do 4 OPEN / 2 LATE'). Registers have real column heads, row titles in condensed bold at about 20px, dates in mono in fixed columns, a NOW divider and a limited measure on the notes. Costs: Chat sets Vera's latest reply at headline size, the bar's numbered keycaps and the footer's shortcut legend add small noise, and Settings labels are mono tracked caps.

Careful typesetting throughout. Home's question is a condensed 40px headline with a true curly apostrophe. Rule heads carry a figure and a link at the right ('5 plans · All plans'). Coming up sets each day as a stacked 'THU / 1' with times in tabular mono and 'in 2 days' right-aligned. Ideas has DRIVE/WAY/FOR/# columns, and Chat's intro breaks deliberately at the colon. Against it: every row title is underlined, Status's leaders run 600px out to the far edge, and the Settings intro is indented off the field edge.

Desk Terminal's steady Plex system, now with a head row on every page. Heads stack a figure over a label ('4 PLANS', '12 IDEAS'), day numerals are bolded inside dates ('Thu 1 Oct'), and Status's Contents plate has leaders to its figures. The tabular due column and NOW rail are good. Weaknesses: the headline question is VT323 at 40px with its tall straight-tick apostrophe, and whole phrases in letterspaced mono ('was due 2 days ago') read wide.

The most ambitious figure-setting yet: Fraunces fractions ('3/4'), a superscript dollar, '2h10 MIN' with a raised h, calendar-leaf dates on To do, big serif day numerals on the month, and contents leaders to counts. Where it works it is beautiful, and the serif, sans, mono and glass faces each have a job. It loses on legibility and hierarchy: 96px low-contrast folios, the drive figure outweighing the idea's name on sparse cards, tracked mono caps on every button, and a truncated Time zone select.

Still solid listing typography: a figure over a caps label in the head column, STATE column heads, dotted leaders to right-aligned values, and the title hung on the text column. Backlit Plate and Quote Board now do the same things with more finish.
Clean one-line rows with WHO/DUE columns and a well-set contents plate. The Home question is a small VT323 line, so the page's largest head is still 'Finish setting up'.
Type is unchanged from Desk Terminal. The new charts bring small 16px VT323 labels and cramped place numbers, which add reading work without adding type quality.
Good column heads and right-aligned tabular figures in the legend tables. Titles and steps are plainer and the pages are less tuned than the newer listing entrants.
It started the title, figure and legend device, which is excellent. Inline tracked mono caps in rows, a near-title first row and the plum cast hold it back; its child Quote Board fixes most of this.

Real poster scale and a clear step system: a heavy lowercase Outfit title beside a square of ink, numbered heads ('01 Where home is') and calendar-leaf dates. But the roughly 110px Home headline shoves the box down, lowercase nav beside a capitalised 'Vera' reads as an error, and geometric display type is furthest of all from the terminal voice.
The contents-line cell heads are a good typographic idea. Tracked caps controls, 46px titles wrapping in narrow cells and half-empty cells hurt it; its Folio child types it far better.
Typography is identical to Track Diagram Relit: an Archivo title over a hairline, DM Sans body and tiny margin dates. Card grids for ideas and tasks keep the measure broken and the figures unaligned.
Decent, but the timetable-margin dates are very small, lists are cards rather than rows, and nothing aligns to a column.

The most typographer-minded idea in the round: a 24px baseline grid on which every block is a whole number of lines, plus a drafting title block. But it is set almost entirely in caps (extended bold heads, tracked condensed labels, 'IN 2 DAYS'). Near one size means little hierarchy, To do shows ISO dates, and two-line rows appear even when a task has no note.

A clear division of jobs, mono for records and sans for speech, and Chat's gutter times are lovely. But Settings help, intros and card titles in Plex Mono 600 are slow and heavy, labels wrap ('Sign-in / and security'), and lists read louder and denser.

The extended thin caps titles are elegant. But the nav and bank heads are tracked caps too, and splitting Status into equal cells of one fact each fragments reading and flattens hierarchy into outlines.

The typed index-card conceit is consistent, but it costs legibility: item titles and 'Save a thought for later' are set in typewriter mono, the nav and Settings list are all tracked mono caps (wrapping to two lines), and the call numbers ('790.1 OAK 01') are figures that mean nothing.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the head device (title, figure in the section colour, stacked mono legend) as the app's standard page head. Chat: set Vera's latest reply at body size (17px/1.5) and put the quote in the head instead ('Vera 4 · last reply 19:53'). Row titles: condensed 600 at 18px, not bold 20, so the page title keeps its lead. Settings field labels: sentence-case sans 13px 500, not mono tracked caps. The '4 shown (up to 100).' line goes in the text face. The bar's key numbers drop to 11px at about 60% ink, or appear only on focus. Align the legend's top line to the figure's cap height and its bottom line to the figure's baseline.

Take the underline off row titles: the whole row is the link, so underline on hover and focus only. On Status, cap each leader row at about 46rem, with values in a fixed right column of about 16rem rather than at the plate's far edge. Align the Settings group intro to the fields' left edge. Keep the stacked 'THU / 1' day column and apply it to To do's due column as well. Set head counts ('5 plans', '12 ideas') as figure 600 plus word 400 in every rule head.

The glass headline needs a real apostrophe: VT323's straight tick looks broken at 40px, so use U+2019 or recast as 'What is on your mind?'. Set due phrases in Plex Sans with only the figures in tabular mono ('was due 2 days ago' in sans, '19:56' in mono) so the column is not letterspaced-wide. Align each head's figure-over-label block to the head's baseline, not its box.

Keep the figure-setting: fractions, superscript currency, the raised h in drive times, calendar-leaf dates, serif day numerals on the month and leaders to counts. Cut folios to about 64px, or raise them to 4.5:1. Ideas cards: title first at 18px/600, drive figure at about 32px, and close the dead space between them. Every button in sentence-case Plex Sans 600, never tracked mono caps. Never truncate a select value; let the field take two columns. Restrict Fraunces to titles, cell heads and figures, which it already nearly is.

Keep the 24px baseline grid and whole-line blocks, which is the best rhythm idea of the round. Drop most of the caps: section heads in sentence-case Archivo 600 at 20px, extended caps only in the sheet title block, labels in 12px 500 small caps at 0.04em. Set To do's dates as 'Sun 27 Sep, 19:56', not ISO. Give a task with no note one grid line. Add one larger step (32-40px) for the page title so the scale has at least four steps.

Cap the Home poster headline at about 72px on two lines so the box sits in the first screen. Use lowercase only in the poster titles and keep the nav in sentence case (or set 'Vera' lowercase too) so the mix does not read as a typo. Set the help and intro text to a 60-65ch measure.

Keep mono for figures, dates, times and table cells only. Return prose (Settings help, intros, the persona text) and the Settings nav to DM Sans. Row names in Plex Mono 500 at the text step, or back in sans with mono metadata. Keep Chat's gutter times, which are the best part.

Item titles in Plex Sans 600, with the typewriter face only for the call-number line. Make the call number real (idea #, drive minutes, days away) rather than Dewey decoration. Nav and the Settings list in sentence case.

judges.notes:
Through the type lens the round has matured. Four entrants now have a real type system: steps, column heads, tabular figures, a figure-over-label head and a controlled measure. The best has come a long way from today's 4.5.

What is now worth making standard:
- The page head as title plus figure plus stacked legend (Quote Board). Every page states its number.
- Rule heads that carry a figure and a link at the right (Backlit Plate).
- Stacked day over date in the date column (Backlit Plate, Quote Board's OCT/1/Thu leaf).
- Mono only for figures, times and dates, in fixed right-aligned columns.
- Curly apostrophes and deliberate line breaks in intros.
- A notes measure of about 60-65ch.

Recurring faults to stop:
- Tracked caps on controls and nav: Folio, Blueprint, Grid Console, Catalogue.
- Whole phrases in letterspaced mono: Joined's 'was due 2 days ago', Monospaced's prose.
- Every row title underlined.
- Leaders stretched across 600px or more to far-edge values.
- VT323's straight apostrophe at headline size.
- Truncated select values.

New ideas worth breeding:
- Folio's figure-setting: fractions, superscript units, the raised h in '2h10', calendar leaves, serif day numerals. It would lift any leader's figures if confined to figures and titles.
- Blueprint's baseline grid: whole-line blocks give the vertical rhythm no other entrant enforces.

The breed I would ask for: Backlit Plate's or Joined's listing typesetting, with Quote Board's page head and Folio's figures used sparingly (fractions in head counts, leaf dates on To do), set on a 24px baseline.

scores.why: Yardstick. 44 of 56 Home targets are under 44px. To do shows ISO dates ('Due 2026-09-27') with no word for late. Ideas has a Restaurants tab and a Kind select that do the same job, plus a Filter press. Memory, Family and Status are unlabelled icons in the bar, and text sits at 17:1 glare.

The easiest page to read tired: 16px body, WHO/DUE heads, amber 'was due' words, a '2 late' link, a NOW divider and 'Edit or snooze' in words. Ideas has one search, one row of one-tap kind keys (Restaurant is a single tap) and a For/Status fold that shows its state. Chat's thread is on the first screen on the phone too, and no target is under 44px. Costs: every row title is underlined, which is noisy to scan; 'Add something to do' sits under the To do list, where a long list would bury it; and Home says '5 plans' over 4 rows.

The best at a glance. Every page opens on its title and figure ('Things to do 4 open, 2 late', 'Status 6 working, 7 off'). The bar names every place and has number shortcuts, explained in the footer. Home's board has a count and a way on in each cell, and To do and Ideas are proper registers with columns and a NOW divider. No small targets. Costs: To do's Show and Ideas' filter sit behind folds, one more click than latched keys. The Settings key loses its word. The month's rows are squat, with small plan names, and the To do figure's amber is also the colour for late.

On desktop it is better than its parent. A head row names each page first. Home's box is a real three-row field in the glass. To do has 'Add something to do' as a primary key in the head, a NOW divider and 'Edit or snooze' in words. Ideas keeps one-tap kind keys with a For/Status fold. But on the phone, Chat opens on the terminal card and conversation list, and the thread starts below the first screen. So the first task, reading Vera's reply, needs a scroll.

Every filter on Ideas, To do and Plans is one mechanism, a latched key with an LED, and nothing is under 44px. Late is amber words. The Contents plate is a fast index. Still weak: Home's box is small in the narrow terminal under a small VT323 question, and To do's add is a fold rather than a key.

Head columns give a figure for every band ('4 open, 2 late'). It has WHO/DUE, a NOW divider, a big Home box and a readable chat. But Ideas mixes mechanisms: kind is a one-tap list, while Status and For are selects that need a Filter press. The radar is pushed to the foot of the column.

Keeps all of Desk Terminal's usability. Status gains a signal legend ('on, waiting, off, needs a look'), and late rows get an amber bar as well as the words, so late is never shown by colour alone. The Ideas map is aria-hidden, its marks are not links, and its labels are small. Home's box moved about 90px lower.

No small targets, and the tables are clear. But Ideas still has the tab and the Kind select for the same thing, and filtering needs a Filter press. On To do, the list starts below the fold, under the filter form and the tube. Status's three narrow tables wrap every row.

Home's track timeline and To do's lamp timeline (amber dates, a 'now' lamp) show late well. But Memory, Family and Status are unlabelled icons, Ideas duplicates tab and select behind a Filter press, and the idea cards show six to a screen.
Its parent with lit lamps, so it works the same way. The glow on Send and the 'now' lamp helps you find them a little. The unlabelled right-hand icons and the duplicate Ideas filters remain.

The same layout, but everything in Plex Mono. Rows and prose read slower and wrap more (month events, settings help), and Home's From row controls dropped to 12.8px. The icon-only right nav and duplicate filters remain.

Home as a map of every page is the best 'where is everything' device. Elsewhere it costs: Ideas has no search or kind filter on the first screen (they sit under the radar). Keys are tracked caps ('ADD AN IDEA'), Chat's input is green VT323 display text, and 20 To do targets are under 44px.

The large figures help. Month numerals make a date easy to find, and drive times are legible. But Ideas cards are mostly empty, with the drive as a figure and a compass arrow that nothing explains ('≈ 2h45 ←'). Search and filters are still off the first screen, keys are caps, and the chat input is VT323.

designs.name: Track Diagram, Monospaced
designs.tagline: Track Diagram Relit re-set: every row, form and figure the family keeps in IBM Plex Mono with a slashed zero, titles and speech alone in proportional faces, and the tubes set as a real terminal's lines.
designs.concept: This is Track Diagram Relit with only its type re-set, so the panel can see what typesetting alone does. Everything the family keeps, lists, puts in tables or fills in is set in IBM Plex Mono with a slashed zero, on four written steps. The proportional faces are kept for the two things that are not data: titles (Archivo, narrowed, unchanged) and speech (DM Sans for Vera's lines, the family's lines, the box you write in and the ways to start). On the glass, VT323 is now set the way a terminal set it: one character cell, rows at the cell's pitch, no tracking, gaps in whole rows, and double-height headlines. It should feel like a calm, exact machine keeping the family's records, with the talking done in a warmer hand.
designs.companions: No colour changes from Track Diagram Relit. Steel-cyan #a7c4d8 is still the family's hand: links, "here", rings and tab caps. Green-black slate trays and plates, cream headings, and the section and kind colours in their lamps and tints are all kept. So is the cobalt wash (#4f66e0 at 2.4) in the greeting's corner, and the exact #6dff9c at full light on the live list (the mark, Send, "mind", the now lamp, the status lamps and the tubes). This mutant's only companion is a face: IBM Plex Mono beside the parent's Archivo and DM Sans, replacing DM Mono, so the page still has four faces.
decisions: The major change is carried by one rule, not by a list of pages. The stylesheet's --sans (which the page uses for every control, label, row and paragraph) now points at IBM Plex Mono. DM Sans is named only where words are said: .said-text, the ask box's textarea, the starters, Home's question, and a page's deck (.lede, .lead, and the 404's line under its title). A deck counts as part of its title, so it stays proportional. Archivo stays on every h1 and h2. As a result Plans, To do, Settings, General, the idea form, Setup, Family, Memory, Wishes and Personality all follow with no rules of their own. I checked each one for sideways scroll: none.

Why IBM Plex Mono and not the parent's DM Mono. DM Mono has no 600 weight, so a row's name would be a synthesised bold. It also has no 'zero' feature: its zero is always slashed. Plex Mono has 400, 500 and 600, a true 'zero' feature, and is the face the panel has rewarded for figures since round 4. One mono replaces the other.

The mono has a written scale of four steps, each with one job. Item is .94rem at 600: the name of a row, card, light or setting, and what you type in a field. Text is .875rem: controls, the bar, links and notes. Small is .8rem: what is said about a thing (its facts), labels, help, kinds and counts. Legend is .72rem: margin stamps, ids and tracked caps. The mono sits a step below the sans it replaces because at equal size its x-height is about the same but its lines run about 30% longer.

A monospaced word space is a full cell and opens holes in a line. On the data, word-spacing is reduced by 0.1em, the way a typesetter sets code in running text. Speech, titles and the glass keep normal spacing. The tighter spacing is also what keeps Send on Home's From row and 'Mount St. Helens day trip' on one line.

The slashed zero (font-feature-settings 'zero') is on every mono word. The page sets many mono words with the font shorthand, which in Chromium resets the features, so the zero is held with !important. It is released for Archivo (which would otherwise slash the zero in 'September 2026'), for DM Sans, and for the glass. Round 12 found a slashed zero blooming into an 8 on the tube, and VT323 has no such feature anyway.

The tubes are re-set as terminal lines. Each tube has one --cell: Next up 1.375rem (1.25rem on the phone), the radar 1.2rem, the spend 1.5rem, the 404 1.25rem. Line-height is 1, so rows sit at the cell's pitch. Letter-spacing is 0 everywhere, because the tracked caps legends broke the column grid. Gaps are whole blank rows: before the prompt, after the radar's count, and before ?NOT FOUND. Reverse video is padded by one cell (1ch) on each side. The block cursor is exactly one cell wide and sits in the next column. The radar's ring labels are in VT323 too. Next up's plan and the spend figure are double-height lines (2 cells), like a VT100's DECDHL lines.

Where a change hurt the page, I bent it. (1) The radar's count stays a single bright row: at double height it wrapped to four rows beside the scope. (2) Timetable stamps went to the legend size (.72rem, lower case) so 'in 2 days 19:56' fits the parent's 7rem margin; at .8rem it ran into its lamp. (3) Home's From row sets its controls at the small step so Send stays on that row. (4) The setup note's inline link got 0.9rem of padding so its target stays 44px in the shorter line, which keeps Home at the parent's 1 target under 44px. (5) Nav icons are pinned at the parent's 1.1rem so they do not shrink with the text. (6) On the phone, To do's 'Edit, complete, or snooze' drops to the small step.

No markup changed. The variant folder is the parent's, copied whole, and removed.txt is empty. Colours, tokens, layout, light and every other rule are the parent's. The parent's track.css and phosphor.css are unchanged apart from comments and whitespace. The type layer is a separate type.css appended after them (variants/r13-mut-1/src/type.css, built by src/build.py), and the palette's css comes to 54,203 characters.
designs.measures: Final full render: 0 hard checks failed, 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 12.75, brand_on_bg 15.18 (#6dff9c exact, brand_neon_vs_today 1.0). Green share of colour: Home 59.8%, Ideas 59.9%, Chat 73.2%, Status 48.1%. Hue entropy: Home 0.514, Ideas 0.447, Chat 0.405, Status 0.434. Kinds dE typical/deuteranopia/protanopia 13.6 / 5.5 / 7.4; sections 12.8 / 5.5 / 5.3. Greeting corner pixel (1150,120) = (24,34,46), the parent's cobalt; bottom-left pool (100,640) = (19,22,18). Smallest text 11.52px, as in the parent. No sideways scroll on any page. Targets under 44px: 1 on each page, desktop and phone, the same as the parent. Home is 1743px tall against the parent's 1766. Palette css is 54,203 characters.
strengths: The change is visible across every page at a glance, not only the greeting. Every row, card, status light, form, nav item and table now reads as the machine's listing in Plex Mono, while Vera's and the family's words stay in DM Sans. Speech and records are told apart by face as well as by bubble.

It is a written system, not a one-off: four faces with one job each, and four mono steps (item, text, small, legend) with stated jobs. It holds on Plans, To do, Settings, General, Setup, Family, Memory and Wishes without a rule per page, because it works through --sans.

The tubes finally read as real terminal lines: an even character grid, rows at the cell pitch, untracked caps, one-cell reverse video, a cursor in the next cell, whole-row gaps, and a double-height 'Pho Oregon' on Next up. The 404 and sign-in readouts look like a DEC screen rather than tracked labels.
The slashed zero makes the family's figures unambiguous (10:00, 09:00, $0.00, '0 open', '4 shown (up to 100)'), and it is kept off the glass and off Archivo, where round 12 found it hurt.

Careful fitting: tighter mono word spacing, a margin stamp size that fits the parent's timetable margin, Send kept on the From row, and 44px targets, smallest text, height and page words all held at the parent's values.
weaknesses: A page mostly in monospace can read as a code editor or a spreadsheet to some eyes. The panel has twice marked down code-like body faces (Recursive). Plex Mono softens this but does not remove it, above all on the prose-heavy Settings help, the Family intro and the persona textarea, where long mono lines are slower to read than DM Sans was.

Mono lines are about 30% longer, so more things wrap than in the parent. The Settings nav's 'Personality / and family' and 'Sign-in / and security' now take two lines. Month-cell events wrap ('Silver Falls / hike'). Idea-card distances often take two lines. On the phone, Next up's double-height title wraps to 'Pho / Oregon'.

The radar's count lost its size: kept as a single bright row to stay terminal-true, it has less hierarchy than the parent's larger count. The spend figure at double height (48px) is also smaller than the parent's 60px.
Home's From row fits by only about 3px at 1280px wide, and it does so because its controls dropped to the small step (12.8px): the select and 'Send where I am' are smaller than the parent's.
The zero is held with a blanket !important on body *, a blunt tool that a future rule could not easily override without the same weight.
Row names at Plex Mono 600 are heavier and wider than the parent's DM Sans 600, so the lists look denser and a little louder, though the colours are unchanged.

designs.name: Desk Terminal, Mapped
designs.tagline: Desk Terminal with its pictures redrawn as plotted charts: the family's places on a map round home, the coming plans against the hours of the day, and every lamp on the page one of four signals, each with one meaning.
designs.concept: This is Desk Terminal with only its graphics changed. The tube no longer shows a radar sweeping over its rings: it plots the family's own data. On Ideas it draws a map: home is lit at the middle, each place is a dot along its real bearing and as far out as the drive, and each dot carries its number from the list. On Home and Plans it charts the coming weeks against the hours of the day. Every small light on every page is now one of four signals, each with one meaning (on, waiting, off, needs a look), so the page feels like the same calm desk with a better instrument on it.
decisions: One chart grammar replaces the radar on every tube: a dotted graticule, labelled axes and rings in VT323, marks drawn as the page's signals, the lines' bloom and 0.35px blur, and the warm-up from a bright line. Two drawings use it: WHERE (the map) and WHEN (the time chart). Both are macros in templates/_ui.html (where_map, when_chart).

WHERE, on Ideas: home is a lit lamp at the middle and north is up. Each place sits along its own bearing, taken from the blip the page is given, on a time scale that opens the near half hour (rings at 15 min, 45 min and 2 h by road). Each place is labelled with its # from the list. Places closer than 9 units share one label ('6 8 10'). A greedy placer in the template tries each label beside its dots, then above or below, then further out on a leader, and never on another label, a dot, home, the compass, the ring words or the edge. The ring words go up the north line on whichever side has fewer places, and the compass takes the other top corner.

The map is square at the left of the glass with the words beside it, the parent's radar-and-words composition at about twice the size. I tried a full-width landscape map first. It wasted the sides, rendered small, and made the Ideas tube 185px taller than the parent's. The square version is about 80px taller.

WHEN, on Home's Next up and on Plans (list and month): each column is a day from today ('now' flag at the left) and the hours 09 to 21 run down the side. Weekends are shaded and Mondays ruled. The next plan is the lamp and pings; the others are dots with a dotted drop to the axis. Each plan's date sits under the axis, staggered when two dates collide. On Plans it replaces the pulse trace. The chart is drawn only when there is a plan to plot, so no empty lit glass is left.

Where a picture needed room: Home's chart sits under Next up's words at full width instead of the 100px radar beside them. The words now fit on one line, but the tube is about 90px taller and Home is 104px longer. The Ideas tube is about 80px taller. The Drive column on Ideas is 1.5rem wider (9rem) to hold the bearing needle.

The idea rows carry the map too: a filled bearing needle (new i-bearing symbol in static/icons.svg, drawn like the map's north arrow) is turned the way each place lies. On a phone the needle stands in for the compass letter, which gives the titles back their room; screen readers still get the words.
The 404 and 403 draw the empty map: a hollow ring where the address should be, with 404 flickering over it (E18). The readout words are kept.

Signals, one meaning each, drawn in CSS to one geometry: the lamp (10px lit disc), dot (7px solid steel), ring (10px, 2px pewter) and bar (12x5 amber). Where each now stands: Status rows (on=lamp, off=ring, partly=bar), judgements, the terminal's foot (Ready=lamp, warn=amber bar, bad=red bar), her Ready state in Chat, the Status tile in the bar, the Messages settings page (copied as templates/settings/messages.html), the NOW lamp and rail stops, the latched-key LED, and late on Home and To do (the bar before 'was due', and before '2 late' on the plate).

Bent rules, stated. (1) Off rings are pewter, not red: 'no key' for Claude is a fact, not an alarm, and red stays for something that has stopped. (2) Latched-key LEDs go from sage to the full lamp, because a latched filter is 'on'. (3) Chat's green track-end ring becomes a lamp, so a lit ring never contradicts 'ring = off'. (4) Status lamps glow with the kit's halo (E20) but only the foot, NOW, her state and the chat end breathe.

Status's Contents plate becomes an annunciator: each band's signals in a row after its name (Who answers ●●●○, Keys ○●○○, Waiting ••, Worth a look ▬ x6), with a one-line key at its foot. The key is aria-hidden; the rows' own words still say each state.

No sweep: a plotted chart does not turn. The motion left is the lamp's breathing, the next or nearest place's ping and the warm-up. Reduced motion stills all of it; more contrast drops the bloom; forced colours outlines the signals.
Words: none changed. 'On the radar', 'Nothing on the radar' and 'Range / Contacts' are kept as idioms. The word-change measure is identical to the parent's (plans 17.7%, home 12.9%, ideas 16.6%).

Colours, type and layout are otherwise the parent's. sheet.css is byte-identical to r12-idea-2's, and all the mutant's rules sit in variants/r13-mut-2/mapped.css (12k characters), carried as the palette's css by variants/r13-mut-2/build.py.
