designs.tagline: Single Quote's trading terminal, one thing set large on every screen, lit and laid in Evening Listing's slate, steel and bone.
designs.concept: A calm evening trading desk. Every page opens on one quote: a condensed Archivo title, its figure in the section colour, and a stacked unit and change line. Everything under it is a register read along a line to fixed columns of facts. One slate rail of numbered keys frames the page. Traced's materials each have one job: green-black glass for what the machine shows, slate for what the family owns and presses, steel reverse video for "here", denim for a link, bone ink for words, and amber only as a caution. The #6dff9c phosphor lights only the live things (the mark and its cursor, the lit number of the key you are on, "mind", Send, the lamps, the now lamp and the tubes), and it lights them at full bloom.
designs.companions: Slate is the main companion, and every page's read content sits on its tray (#10161a): Home's three board cells, the Ideas listing, the To do register, the chat thread, Status's three monitors and the month. The zebra (#161d22) marks the lead To do row. The keycaps (#252d33 to #1c2328, edge #3a454c), the wells (#1b2126 with #5b6570 edges, for ticks, checkboxes and the From select) and the bar (#0f1417, glass with a blur over the scroll) are slate too. Steel (#6b8396 reverse video with dark ink and a #9cc4dc cap) means "here" everywhere: the current key, the tabs, the settings nav, the menu, the picked option, and today on the month and the date chip. Denim (#9db6d6, underlined, in the text face) marks every way on: All plans, All 4, All 12, Add an idea, Change a key, Change the limit and Edit. Steel-blue (#84a0c4) is the accent of Home, Vera, Status and Settings (the title tiles and Status's figure), and legends are steel #a4b0c2. A cobalt second light (#4f60e6 at washGlow 2.4) sits in the greeting's far corner, opposite the green pool. Words are bone #d4cfc4 with cream headings #ebe6da. The family's chat slips are slate #1f272e under a steel cap, and Vera's are green-black glass #111712 with a faint phosphor edge. Monitor cases are graphite #2e3337. Amber (--warn, the same #ffb850 as the family section and the restaurant kind) is only an edge, a word or a figure: the 3px setup edge, "was due", "2 late" (now a link), and NEEDS A LOOK.
decisions: Structure from Single Quote (r12-wild-4), colour from Evening Listing, Traced (r12-idea-1), as the first draft set it out. Every plum literal was re-tinted to slate at the same lightness, and Traced's colour code became the sheet's own tokens (--band, --zebra, --rule, --link, --rev, --rev-cap, --well, --glass, --row-wash, and now --warn).

One row of chrome (this revision). The mark with its E2 cursor, keys 1 to 6, a hairline, keys 7 to 9 and the 0 settings key now share one 3.25rem glass rail. The key you are on is steel reverse video with its number lit #6dff9c in a dark #0b0e0c socket, using the E20 halo as a text glow; this replaces the hollow-ring LED. The command path moved to the crumbs over the title ('> SETTINGS', '> IDEAS', '> PLANS', with a sage '>'). The dashed Alt chip is gone, and the footer now carries a keycap legend: Shortcuts: [Alt] and a key's number · [Alt][⇧] in Firefox · [⌃][⌥] on a Mac. On a phone the six places go along the foot as before, and the household's three keys and the settings key sit in the bar as icons.

Every list is a register. Ideas is one 54px line to an idea: #id, the kind legend in its colour, the title at --t-lead, the drive in two fixed sub-columns (the time right-aligned, the compass point beside it, under a FROM HOME / by road, est. head), and FOR in the text face. Ten ideas show above the fold, against 4.5 before. To do is one line to a task under WHO and DUE heads: tick well, #id and title, who, 'was due Sun 27 Sep, 19:56' in amber or 'due Thu 01 Oct, 19:56', a bell and time only when a reminder is set, and a pencil 'Edit' key whose form opens across the whole row (::details-content, display: contents). A NOW hairline with the page's one breathing E20 lamp sits between the late and upcoming rows.

Home's board has level feet. Each cell is legend and figure on one baseline, its one thing large, a tape, then a foot pushed to the bottom with grid-template-rows ... 1fr auto. The feet read 'All plans →', '2 late → … All 4 →' (amber, linking to ?late=1, which this tasks.html copy filters as Traced's does) and '+ Add an idea … All 12 →'. The To do tape says 'was due yesterday' in words.

Next up is sized to its words. The 21rem min-height is gone and the radar sits beside the words (grid-row 1 / 3), so the tube is about 16rem instead of 21rem and has no empty lit glass. On a phone the scope readout is hidden, the radar drops to 6.5rem, and the title steps down so 'Pho Oregon' fits on one line.

The Ideas monitor is a quote on the glass. ON THE RADAR spans the top, the count '10' is set 3.4rem over 'places / from home' beside a 9rem scope, and the nearest and furthest lines sit under it. The tube is about 22rem tall instead of 31rem. On the glass, 'Bi‑Mart' keeps its hyphen whole (U+2011) and '[18 MIN NW]' will not split.

Status now quotes its lamps like every other page: 'Status 6 / WORKING / ▸ 7 OFF'. The quote's right half is the lamp panel, set as three banks (4 | 4 | 5, divided by rules and captioned ANSWERS 3/4, KEYS 1/4, LINKS 2/5) at full width, so the strip indexes the monitors below. Each light is one line: its name on the left and its state on the right in dim. The monitors are about 30% shorter, and 'Change a key' and 'Change the limit' are 44px denim keys with arrows.

Type roles are tighter. .stamp is no longer capitalised (letter-spacing .01em), so rows read 'Sun 04 Oct 13:00'. Capitals stay on eyebrows, legends, column heads, units, the change line and labels. Names and places (tape .who, idea-card, kids, task who, idea FOR) moved from Plex Mono to 400 14px Archivo in --dim with tabular figures, and Plex is kept for figures and moments. Home's lead To do line ('Alex was due 2 days ago') is a sentence, so it is in the text face.

Chat has one grammar for every slip. Who and when sit on one line above the words, the words run to a 60ch measure, and the slips take their width from their words (Vera's on the left, the family's on the right). The family's initials are plain letters on slate, no longer ringed keys; the steel cap on the slip says 'family'. The newest line is still set large in cream.

I restored the bar's glass (backdrop blur) on the desktop. Without it, Chromium drew the page's text with coloured subpixel fringes, and that alone moved the measured green share from about 65% to 37% and made the bone ink look fringed. The phone's bar is solid, so the fixed foot row can sit on the viewport, and the foot row carries the blur instead.

Light: glow 0.9, screenGlow 1.0 and topGlow 1.0 are unchanged, and the phosphor list stays at full strength. It gained two live things: the lit number in the current key's socket and the now lamp on To do. The page's halos keep Traced's 0.9.

strengths: There is one system on every page. Each page has one quote (Status and the month included), one row of keys with a lit number for 'here', and one register drawing (Ideas, To do, the Status lights, Home's tapes) with fixed fact columns and column heads. Both the sheet's six rules and the code follow them.

The page gives more to content. There is one 52px rail instead of 94px of chrome, 10 ideas above the fold instead of 4.5, one-line To do rows instead of 108px ones, Status's board on the first screen, and Home 70px shorter.

Late reads the same on every surface: amber words ('was due …') and edges, '2 late' as a link to the late ones on Home and in To do's quote, and a NOW hairline with the page's only live lamp between late and upcoming.

The phosphor stays on the short list at full strength: mark and cursor, the lit number in the socket, 'mind', Send, Next up and the radar monitors with bloom, blur and scanlines, the breathing lamps and the now lamp. Everything solid is matte slate, steel, denim or bone.

The typesetting is cleaner. Moments are in Plex as written ('Sun 04 Oct 13:00') and names are in Archivo text. Caps are kept for legends and heads. Drive figures sit in right-aligned tabular sub-columns, the chat runs to a 60ch measure, and legends sit on the figure's baseline in the board cells.

Usability: 0 small targets on every page, the Tab order matches the drawing (skip, mark, keys 1 to 9, 0, the box, From, Send), one chevron for every list control, the task edit form opens in place, and the footer carries a real keyboard legend.
weaknesses: Status is still the calmest page (hue entropy .347, 52% green). Its colour is steel, slate and green only, which suits a health page but may still read as monochrome to the owner's lens.

Home's board cells are level at the foot, but the To do cell keeps about 90px of empty tray above its foot (Coming up about 40px), because Lately added sets the height. Long To do titles in the tape wrap to two lines next to 'was due yesterday'.

At 1280px the bar is full edge to edge. The settings key gives up its word ('Settings' becomes a gear, 0 and a chevron) so every place keeps its name. The critic asked for icons on Memory, Family and Status instead; that only happens below 72rem.
The footer's shortcut legend adds words to every page (Plans 20%, 404 19% word difference). It is also only a guess at each browser's access-key modifier.

Amber is still one hue with two jobs visually: the family section, the restaurant kind legend and icon, and caution. Only the code parts them (--warn); a palette would need a new hue to part them on the page.
The phone's Next up tube still runs past the first screen, and the phone Ideas rows take three lines each.

HOME: the tile grid gets rows ending in 1fr auto, with the go-links in a foot on one level line. '2 late →' is an amber link to /tasks?late=1. The tape says 'was due yesterday'. The kids' strip drops the per-kid '0 open' when the figure is 0 (screen readers still hear 'nothing open'). firstDraft.name: Phosphor Blueprint
firstDraft.concept: Every page becomes a sheet from a set of architectural drawings. A drafting grid (24px cells, the height of one line of text) lies under a framed sheet with zone marks along its edges, a title block at the head of each page and one at its foot. Dated lists become schedules read across in rows, the kinds of idea become a legend of hatched swatches, the month becomes a structural grid with bubbled columns and weeks, and Settings becomes the drawing index. The CRT is the machine drawn on that sheet: the only things lit are the monitors, her screen, the mark and cursor, the one primary action, the box being typed in, focus and the live lamps, so the phosphor glows at full strength against a calm, grounded drawing.

designs.name: Signal Catalogue
designs.tagline: A walnut-and-brass card catalogue wired for sound: typed index cards with call numbers, drawer labels in brass holders, and a green scope that draws the weeks ahead as a signal.
designs.concept: The page is a walnut-and-brass card cabinet on a green-black ground. Everything the family keeps is filed on a dark typed index card, with a headline rule in its kind's colour, a brass call number and a rod hole at the foot. Each part of the site is a drawer, found by a label in a riveted brass holder; manila is kept for the drawer you are in. Sound is the ornament and the phosphor is the machine's life: a scope draws the next four weeks as one pulse per plan, LED meters count down to each plan, every busy day on the month carries a pulse, and Vera is a glowing waveform. Bright green lives only where the machine is alive: the mark, the one primary key, the card being typed on, focus, lamps and the tubes, which carry the original light in full.
designs.companions: Brass (label #d2ae75, hue 74) is the main companion and does the hardware: every typed label, eyebrow, date and call number, the drawer-label holders, rivets and flanges, the rules under panel titles, the signal lines, the pulses on the month, chevrons and the monitors' maker's plates. Manila (brass and paper ink, calmed toward the card and then 20% toward walnut: #a08e74, its dark ink 6.3:1) now has one job only, where you are: the page's plate, the bar's (or phone tab bar's) current drawer, and the current guide tab. Every other drawer label (Home's Coming up, To do, Lately added, The kids' wishes, the month on Plans, each kid on Wishes) is dark walnut with its words typed in manila (5.8:1). Walnut (bar #18130c, bezel #261e15) is the cabinet: the top rail, the tab bar, Home's hero, the drawer labels, the settings drawer stack, the now-opaque save bar and the monitor cases. Carbon card stock (surface #1c1813) with paper ink #e8e2d7 for the cards. Muted terracotta (seasons) is a real index card's red headline rule on the ask card, the enquiry slip and the new-idea card; faint blue (plans at 10-18%) is their ruled lines. The kind colours sit at guide-card chroma on tabs, headline rules and kind labels. Amber is kept for today, anything that needs a look, and the family's initials, now typed on dark stock rather than filled.
decisions: Clean sheet (118.6 KB), with overrides of six templates (_ui, home, ideas, tasks, 404, 403) and five of its own SVGs (wave, wave-trail, burst, tick and the new pulse). removed.txt is empty. The page's words change by at most 0.6% (Ideas, for the real 'Catalogue enquiry' eyebrow).

Type system from one superfamily with two caps steps, written once as custom properties. LABEL is 500 0.72rem/1.3 at +0.12em: eyebrows, field labels, call numbers, dates, kinds, th, tags, .rel. KEY is 500 0.8rem/1.2 at +0.08em: the bar, guide tabs, drawer labels, the settings drawers, setup steps. In mixed case: 0.84 for links and small, 0.94 for meta, and 1rem for body and every card title (Plex Mono, -0.015em, text-wrap: balance). Panel titles are 1.12, the question 1.6, and the plate 1.3-1.65. IBM Plex Mono types, IBM Plex Sans is read, VT323 only on the tubes.
Manila is rationed to where you are. The page plate is smaller (2px holder, clamp 1.3-1.65rem), so the phosphor wins first look and the plate second.

Home is one cabinet row. Each drawer is a label, a signal line (its burst at 8%, 55% or 30% along, so the three no longer read as a stamp) and a dark well. The wells stretch to one foot line, so a drawer with fewer cards reads as half empty. The calendar note is filed at the foot of Coming up under a tear line, and Add an idea is a dashed blank card at the foot of Lately added.

The rod hole sits on every card-proportioned filed card: Home's slips, the lately-filed cards, and the cards on Ideas and To do. Ledger rows (the plans list), panels and settings' guide cards have none.

Next up's scope was redrawn. Pulses rise up to 44 units, the sooner the taller. The trace sits on y=58 in a 240x86 view, with now, 1w, 2w, 3w and 4w labelled under the swing ('now' anchored left), and the tube is a grid so the scope sits at its foot. Days come from views' days_away when it is present and otherwise from the radar blips' geometry, computed once for the scope and the meters alike.

Plans month: the month is a walnut drawer label with its signal line running to Earlier and Later. Events are small index cards (a plans-coloured top edge, a typed title, the time in brass). Every day holding a plan carries the scope's own pulse at its foot, two pulses for two plans, lit green on today.

To do: one number per card. The corner call number is TASK (decoration) over #4, the number the family says to her, and the h2 holds only the title. The raw ISO due date is worded as the page words a day ('Due Sunday 27 September, 19:56'). The template uses views' due and late (relative, amber when overdue) as soon as task_row carries them.

New idea is the card being typed. It has a blank call number '000 NEW', the title typed on the heading line above the terracotta rule, the description on blue ruled lines (field-sizing), a lit margin line and rule while typing, and the whole card lit on focus-within.

The Ideas enquiry heading is a real

carrying the inset terracotta rule, with faint blue ruled lines under the fields. The radar's bracketed distances no longer break.

44px reach without bigger drawings: the task tick (1.6rem) and checkboxes (1.25rem) are drawn as their content box, with a transparent border as the reach and negative margins giving the room back. Forced-colors rules draw them with system colours. Menu rows, starters, the mic, selects, folds, drawer-label links, tabs, bar places, crumbs, kid rows and setup steps are 2.75rem. On Home a whole plan slip is its link.
Controls in character: base-select picker as a small drawer, a brass chevron, fields as platens that light, a checkbox that lights in lit with a halo, and a 2px brand focus ring everywhere.

The phosphor kit stays in full on the tubes (glass, three-halo VT323, 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen, vignette, inverse, cursor, spill, power lamp, beam and flare), on the mark and its cursor, the primary key and the lamps. glow, screenGlow and topGlow stay at 1.0, and --shadow is never 'none'.

Bright green per mille: Home 3.88, Ideas 7.86, Chat 4.53, Status 0.50. CIEDE2000 minimum distance for the kinds: 17.5 typical, 7.0 deuteranopia, 9.5 protanopia; for the sections: 18.6, 7.0, 6.7. Greeting corners: the brass wash at (1150,120) samples (32,32,20). The green glow's corner is now at (100,480) and samples (22,34,22), because the greeting ends near y=520 and the old (100,640) sample now lands in the notices row: (28,24,19). Manila is #a08e74, with its ink at 6.3:1 and as text on walnut at 5.8:1. Click targets under 44px: Home 8 of 56 (was 45), To do 1 of 97 (was 45), Chat 3 of 29, General 1 of 48, Ideas 15 of 49 (the card titles, whose whole card is the link). Smallest text 11.52px, no sideways scroll on any page, and the page's words change by at most 0.6% (Ideas). Sheet is 118,642 characters.
strengths: One system with jobs that hold on every page, including pages the harness doesn't render: the plans list, an idea's page, Wishes and Family all take the drawer labels, index cards, brass labels and guide-letter initials without their own rules.
Manila now means only 'you are here' (plate, bar or tab-bar current, current guide tab). Every other label is dark walnut in a brass holder, so the phosphor wins first look.

Sound does real work as the ornament. Scope pulses show how soon, LED meters show how near, the month's pulses mark the busy days (lit on today), signal lines run to the way on, and Vera is a waveform.

The original phosphor light is back in full where the machine is: the tubes (bloom, blur, scanlines, sheen, beam, flare, cursor, power lamp), the mark, the primary key, lamps, the card being typed on and focus. Everything else is walnut, brass and card stock.
Home is one cabinet row: three wells ending on one line, each drawer's foot doing a job (a note, a blank card).
The typesetting is tightened: two caps steps and one card-title step as variables, mixed-case links, tabular figures, balanced titles, ledes at 60ch, and baseline-aligned date rows.
Controls in character, with a real 44px reach for the tick and checkboxes without enlarging their drawing. Forced-colors, reduced-motion, more-contrast and print are covered.
Three typed cards share one grammar: the ask card, the enquiry slip and the new-idea card each have the question or title above a red headline rule, blue ruled lines, and light while typed on.
weaknesses: To do cannot yet say 'was due 2 days ago' in amber or carry a meter: the page is not given today, and the harness doesn't let me change views. The worded date is a fallback. The template already uses row.due and row.late when views.task_row carries them, as task_brief does for Home.
Home's scope and meters still read days back from the radar blips' geometry unless views adds days_away to entry_row. It is exact to a tenth of a day, but indirect.
The 44px reach for the tick and checkboxes uses a transparent border and negative margins: it works and is tested in forced colors, but it is a trick that a later edit could easily break.
The walnut drawer labels with manila words (5.8:1) are quiet, so at a glance a drawer may be found by its signal line more than by its label.
The To do well on Home can stand tall and mostly empty when there are only a few tasks. That is honest, but it is a lot of dark.
The month label on Plans is 1rem, a deliberate exception to the 0.8rem drawer-label step.
The new-idea description and the ask box are fields drawn only as ruled lines, with no box edge. It is in character, but less obviously a field to someone who expects a box.
The page still spends a lot of caps (bar, drawer labels, field labels, kinds, eyebrows); this revision only took the links and counts out of them.
The sheet grew from 105 KB to 118.6 KB.

Home's section-head h2 (Coming up, To do, Lately added, The kids' wishes) is now a dark walnut label with manila words, a brass-dim holder and two rivets like the bar's drawer fronts, at the KEY step. 5 Typesetting. The two caps steps (LABEL 0.72/+0.12em, KEY 0.8/+0.08em) are written as custom properties and applied across eyebrows, labels, call numbers, kinds, tags, th, .rel, crumbs, OK, and to the bar, tabs, drawer labels, settings nav and setup steps. Card titles are one 1rem Plex Mono at -0.015em, balanced, which fixes the 'Silver / Falls' orphan. .section-head and .section-links links are mixed-case Plex Mono at 0.84 ('All plans →'). .count lost its caps and, in tasks.html, its trailing full stop. .brief-more is mixed case. Panel titles and fold summaries are one 1.12 step, ledes are 60ch, and date rows are baseline-aligned.

6 Phone chat. Below 40rem the thread takes 100%, the family's initials hide (their names are typed in .said-by), and Vera's screen shrinks to 1.6rem. On every width, family initials are dark card stock with an amber typed letter and a brass edge; the Family page's tiles follow the same rule, with pink letters for kids.

7 Controls and targets. The starters' focus ring is lifted above the ask card. The following are 2.75rem: bar places, section-head and section-links links, tabs, menu rows, starters, the mic, the ask select, .more summaries, crumbs, settings nav, kid rows and setup steps. The checkbox is drawn at 1.25rem with a 44px reach, and so is the tick at 1.6rem. Field mics are 44px in the field's corner. The save bar is solid walnut. On Home each plan slip is its link. in ideas.html, carrying the terracotta rule inset to the content with 0.6rem below. The promised blue ruled lines are drawn under the fields at 10%.

Beyond the notes: the wish-list headings got an icon gap, the setup slip's ruled background became row rules to fit 44px rows, forced-colors rules were added for the new tick and checkbox drawing, and the tagline now says walnut (the old one said oak).

Declined or bent: the relative due, amber and meter on To do (needs views; the template is ready); days passed from views (not reachable here; the template prefers it when present); burst.svg in the month cells (replaced by the scope's pulse shape for one signal language); the rod hole on ledger rows (left off, since they are not cards).
crit: 1. Ration and calm the manila. It samples at about (194,175,144), roughly 9:1 on the ground, and it now labels things that are not 'the drawer you are in', so a pale plate wins second look on every page. Apply the design's own rule: solid manila only for where you are (the bar or tab-bar current, the h1 plate, the current .tabs a). Make Home's .section-head h2 (Coming up, To do, Lately added, The kids' wishes) a dark label in a brass holder: background: var(--walnut); color: var(--manila); border-color: var(--brass-dim). On settings subpages, draw .settings-nav a[aria-current] as a dark label with an inset 2px brass edge and a lit icon: today General shows 'GENERAL' twice in manila within 200px. Knock --manila down about 20% toward walnut (for example color-mix(in oklab, <current> 78%, var(--walnut))), which keeps manila-ink above 6:1. Shrink the plate: .title-row h1 { font-size: clamp(1.3rem, 2.6vw, 1.65rem) } and .title-row { border-width: 2px; padding: .4rem 1.1rem .38rem .5rem }. The phosphor then wins first look on every page, as it should.

2. Carry the catalogue and the signal onto Plans, To do and the form. They are the plainest pages. Plans month (plans.png): type .month-head h2 as a drawer label with the burst signal line running to Earlier and Later. Turn .event slips into index cards (border-left: 0; border-top: 2px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--plans) 70%, var(--surface)); title in var(--type)). Give each day holding a plan a pulse at the cell foot, in brass, and in lit green for today: table.month td:has(.event)::after with the same burst.svg mask as .section-head::after. To do (todo.png): show one number per card. '#4 ·' in the h2 repeats 'Task 004' in the corner, so drop one, or make the call number readable. Replace the raw 'Due 2026-09-27 19:56' with Home's relative time and meter(), amber when overdue, the way the Home checklist already says 'was due 2 days ago'. New idea (form.png) is literally the card being typed. Give its panel the ask card's grammar: the terracotta headline rule under #title, the blue ruled lines of .ask textarea in Description, a blank call number ('000 NEW') in the corner, and the lit edge on :focus-within.

3. Make Home's three drawers one cabinet row. Lately added has no well while Coming up and To do sit in .agenda and .checklist wells, so give .idea-cards the same well. Set .cabinet { align-items: stretch } and .drawer { display: flex; flex-direction: column } .drawer > :is(.agenda, .checklist, .idea-cards) { flex: 1 } so the wells end on one line: the To do well stops about 210px above the others, and an empty dark well reads honestly as a half-empty drawer. Put the rod hole on every filed card or on none: today only .cards > .card has one, .idea-card has none, and .tasks > .card::after hides it. 'Lately added' crushes its signal line to a stub under '+ ADD AN IDEA  ALL 12'. Move Add an idea into the well as a dashed slip at its foot, or give .section-head::after { min-width: 3.5rem }. Vary the burst per drawer (for example a --burst-at offset of 8%, 30% or 55%), because three identical 120px stamps side by side read as a rubber stamp rather than a signal.

4. Fix the scope in the Next up tube (home.png, motion-on). Today's pulse sits at x=18, exactly on the 'now' label, and strikes through it. 3w has a tick at x=171 but no label, so the time base looks broken. In the scope macro, move the labels to y=86, anchor 'now' at x=4 with text-anchor start, and add <text x=171>3w</text>. Fill the empty band between '4 more on the radar' and the trace: raise the amplitude to 'h': [44 - d*1.1, 9]|max, cut the viewBox to 0 0 240 80, and set .next-up .crt-tube { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr } with the .scope at align-self: end. Pass each plan's days from views rather than from the radar's geometry.

5. Typesetting: collapse the drifted scale. The typed caps labels use five sizes (0.72, 0.75, 0.76, 0.78 and 0.8rem) and six trackings (0.04 to 0.12em). Make them two steps. One is a label step, 500 0.72rem/1.3 at +0.12em, for eyebrows, labels, call numbers, dates and th. The other is a key step, 500 0.8rem/1.2 at +0.08em, for the bar, tabs, drawer labels and settings nav. Card titles use 0.98, 1, 1.02 and 1.06rem: make them one 1rem Plex Mono at -0.015em with text-wrap: balance. That also fixes the 'Book the campsite at Silver / Falls' orphan in the three-column To do drawer. The caps budget is spent: the bar, h1, drawer labels, kinds, .rel, eyebrows and form labels are all uppercase. So set .section-head a and .section-links a in mixed case ('All plans →', 'All 4 →') at 0.84rem Plex Mono, and let .count ('4 SHOWN (UP TO 100).') drop its caps and its trailing full stop.

6. On the phone, chat bubbles are squeezed to about 254px of 390. Two 2.25rem avatars plus .thread > li { max-width: 88% } leave 'What should we do this / weekend?' at about 22 characters a line. Below 40rem: .thread > li { max-width: 100% }, .said-them .avatar { display: none } (the name is already typed in .said-by), and Vera's .presence in the thread at 1.6rem. On every width, the filled amber family tiles (.said-them .avatar { background: var(--people) }) are the loudest non-green things in the thread. Make them dark card stock with an amber typed initial and a brass edge, like the guide letter on a drawer.

Add .starters a:focus-visible { position: relative; z-index: 1 }. Targets: 45 of 56 on Home and 45 of 97 on To do are under 44px. At desktop set .places a { min-height: 2.75rem } (40px today). Set .section-head a, .section-links a and .tabs a to min-height 2.75rem, as inline-flex with align-items: center. Make the checkbox 1.25rem, with label.check padded to 44px. firstDraft.name: Signal Catalogue
firstDraft.concept: The page is a library card cabinet on a green-black ground. What the family keeps is filed on dark index cards, each with a typed heading, a headline rule in its kind's colour, a Dewey call number in the corner and a rod hole at the foot. Each part of the site is a drawer, found by its manila label in a brass holder with a pull under it. Everything else is warm and material: walnut, brass, carbon card, paper ink.

designs.name: Dessau Phosphor
designs.tagline: Every page a poster: its name set large and lowercase beside a square of its ink, its one live figure glowing on a round green screen, and four shapes with four jobs (the circle is light, the square the family's, the bar the page's, the triangle what needs a look).
designs.concept: The family's page set as Bauhaus posters, lit by one green tube. Every page opens with its name in lowercase Outfit beside a solid square of the section's print ink, and the page's one live figure glows on a round phosphor screen. Everything else is matte: square slate cards, bone type, dimmed inks, thick bars. The page should feel bold, calm and printed, with the full original phosphor light (bloom, blur, scanlines, sweep, afterglow) only where the machine speaks.
designs.companions: Slate blue at OKLCH hue 259 (#9fbff2, `accent`) is the page's structure on Home, Vera, Status and Settings: the poster's square and the foot of its bar, section numerals, links, the current-place bar, and the Save bar. It is now also the settings menu's top bar on every page (`--slate`). Slate also tints every surface, line and field (#13171e cards, #0f1116 fields). Bone (#e5dfd3 ink, #eee7d9 headings) is the type. Five section and kind inks are the Bauhaus trio dimmed to print colours: mauve for ideas, sea-glass for plans, ochre for to do, rose for wishes and shows, sage for outing. They appear only as solid squares, bars and numerals, never as glow, and a filled square is now mixed 78% ink to 22% ground so it reads as printed rather than lit. Amber (`people`) is for what needs a look (the triangle, an amber tube), for family faces and for late dates. Brick is for the seasons. Warm graphite #24211c is the family's chat bubble, beside her slate one.
decisions: Clean sheet (variants/r13-wild-3/sheet.css, about 102 KB), my own templates and my own 54-symbol sprite drawn from circles, squares, bars and triangles. Nothing is removed (removed.txt is empty) and the page's words differ by 0.6% at worst.

Four shapes with four jobs on every page. The circle is light: tubes, her screen, lamps, the mark, today, the mic, the radio dot. The square is the family's: cards, fields, date leaves, ticks, faces, kind tiles. The bar is the page's: the poster's base, section heads, the current place, tabs, the Save bar, buttons. The triangle is what needs a look. Corners are square and only light is round. A labelled key of the four closes every footer.

The posters now come in three sizes, chosen by what the page is. POSTER (clamp up to 8.75rem) is for a page that is only its greeting: Home's question, sign-in, 404/403. BILL (new, clamp(3rem, 1.2rem + 4.6vw, 5.75rem)) is for a section's working page. DISPLAY (2.9rem) is for a page under another, detected by crumbs (.is-sub). All three come from the one page_head macro, and every title hangs from one top line (align-items: start).

The poster's round screen shows the page's one live figure. The figure is sized by its length in container units (len-1 to len-6, cqi) so it fills the glass at any size, and a long word under it steps down. Plans (list and month) share one reading of the next plan through `round_screen({'plan': entry})`: its time when it is today ('NEXT PLAN / 17:00 / TODAY'), otherwise 'NEXT IN / 2 / DAYS'. To do shows 'STILL / 4 / TO DO'. Status shows the day's spend and turns amber or red near and past the limit. Settings shows how many parts need a look, in amber.

Kleinschreibung is now a rule that holds on any page. The posters and the places (the bar, the tabs) are lowercase. A proper name in them keeps its capital through a `words()` macro that marks names with .name: internal capitals (AI, FamilyDB), a capitalised word after the first (what Vera remembers), a possessive first word (Maya's wishes), a short list of companies, and a `proper` flag (Vera, a person's page). Headings, labels, buttons, summaries and sentences keep the case they are written in.

The phosphor light is the kit's, at full strength and only on round and lit things. The tubes have VT323 blurred 0.35px under three halos, 1-in-3 scanlines, sheen, falloff, an 80px spill, a case lit from above, and a power lamp. The radar has its sweep, afterglow, blips and ping. Her screens have falling glyphs. There is a two-layer halo on 'mind' and on the mark. The lit button has its ring and a pool of light under it. The box being typed in glows. Lamps breathe, the caret blinks, and afterglow is 1.2s out and 0.12s in. Round glass opens out of a dot.

Home's question is lit from below: the light pools under 'mind' where the box begins, rises round the letters and spills out past the box, through faint scanlines. The greeting's bar is plain grey because Home has no square of ink.

Grounded colour away from the light. The squares of ink are printed (78% ink), the lamps that are off are dark rather than red, and red is kept for real failures under Needs attention. The sign-in poster sets FamilyDB as the bar's own mark, in DM Mono 500 with the lit caret.

Type system: poster, bill, display, h2 at 1.55rem, lede at 1.15rem/44ch, body at 1rem/1.55, small at 0.875rem, and label at 0.75rem Outfit 600 caps tracked 0.16em. Outfit sets names, DM Sans sentences, DM Mono the machine's small voice, and VT323 appears only on tubes. Figures are tabular, headings use text-wrap: balance and paragraphs text-wrap: pretty. Poster tracking is -0.045em, and a heading that opens a form is 1.15rem, quieter than what the page lists.

Greeting pixels: corner (1150,120) = (10,15,13), since there is no wash drawn in that corner; lower-left glow (100,640) = (22,43,29), up from (17,31,22); under 'mind' (600,395) = (29,56,39). strengths: Home's greeting is the most distinctive in the tournament and is kept at poster size. 'what's on your mind?' is lowercase with 'mind' lit under a two-layer halo, and its light now visibly pools under the word and spills past the box. The eye goes question, then box, then the lit Send bar.

The poster system now fits the page it heads. The working pages start about 150px sooner than before (To do, Status, Settings, the form and General all open within the first screen). The chat's Send row is back above the fold at 1280x900, and every title hangs from the same top line.

Each round screen carries a live meaning, with the kit's full light. Plans' list and month agree on how soon the next plan is. Status is amber or red near and past the limit, and Settings is amber with its count. The figure fills the glass at any size.
The four shapes with four jobs hold on every page shot and on pages outside the set (Plans list, Wishes, Memory, Connections, checked on a private server). The footer's key names them.

Names are right everywhere. The rule is simple enough to hold on any template: only posters and places are lowercase, and the words() macro keeps capitals on AI, FamilyDB, Vera, Telegram, Google and the kids' names.

The palette stays grounded away from the light. Slate cards, bone type, printed squares of ink, dark lamps for what is off and red only for real failures give a calm page where only the machine glows.
The phone's Home puts the Next up words on the first screen, with a small scope tucked behind their corner.
weaknesses: To do's screen still shows the open count ('STILL / 4 / TO DO'), a figure the page also prints, not the late count the critic asked for. The tasks view gives the template no clock, so a template cannot tell late from on time. That needs views.task_row to pass `late`, as Home's view does.

The Kleinschreibung is now narrower than the first draft. Section heads, buttons and labels are in sentence case, so the lowercase Bauhaus voice lives only in the posters, the bar and the tabs. That was the price of keeping names right on every template. Some will miss the all-lowercase buttons.

The words() name detection is a heuristic. A name that begins a title without a possessive or the `proper` flag, and is not a known company, would still be lowercased. The known cases (chat, a person's page, kids' wishes, Settings' AI) are covered.
Round screens are smaller (about 131px at 1280). The long words under the figure ('NEED A LOOK', '0% OF $2.00') are set at about 14px VT323, and on Status that is small for blurred phosphor type.
A section's poster with no lede (Plans) leaves a tall empty band beside its name, because the round screen is taller than the title.
The greeting's top-right corner is plain ground (10,15,13). The slate `wash` token is not drawn there, so Home's second light is only the underlight.

Pages under another (General, New idea, Connections) have a small square of ink and a short foot on their bar at display size, so their posters are quieter than a section's by design. Some may read that as timid.

designs.name: Grid Console
designs.tagline: The family's control panel standing on the Grid: equal cells drawn by their outlines, light trails for every rule, and the phosphor only where the machine speaks.
designs.concept: Every page is a console on a twelve-column lattice. The family's things sit in banks of equal outlined cells, like keys on a panel, and hatched blank plates close any row a bank leaves open. A light-trail spine leaves the title (or her screen, on Home), turns into every bank at a lit square node, and runs down the gutter to the horizon at the foot. There the column guides run straight into a perspective Grid floor drawn at the same pitch. The old green tube is kept whole inside every monitor and on its own small floor. The page is calm, exact and dark, lit in phosphor only where the machine speaks.
designs.companions: Hue-202 steel teal is the Grid's own colour: the column guides, the floor and horizon, cell outlines (#25393b), the label tier (#8fb4b7, restored this round), and the spine, links and title tiles on Home, Vera, Status and Settings (#77ced5). Amber (#eeb46e) is for today and anything needing a look: today's month cell and its TODAY tag, the setup bank, late tasks, Needs a look. It is also the family's side of the chat: their cell outlines, their initials and now their names in the said-by row. Each section keeps its own lower-chroma colour, used only in thin things: its bank's trail, the corner mark on each cell, its spine node, its nav key's underline, its title tile, and the floor lines at the foot of its pages. Plans are pale blue #9bcafe, ideas lilac #bea0f0, to do wheat #f3e18e, wishes rose #e79cbe, seasons coral #f5886d and outing sage #b8e9ae. The bright #6dff9c stays on the mark and cursor, the one primary key per view, the glowing word "mind", focus, live lamps, the tubes, her screen, the edge of her chat cells, and her name, lit with the E1 halo. A calmer lit green (#76e699) takes the box being typed in, a field cell's outline while you write in it, ticked boxes, OK and done badges, and the steel keys' hover.
decisions: A clean sheet (variants/r13-wild-4/sheet.css, about 140 KB) with its own templates: home, chat, ideas, tasks, plans_month, settings, login, 404 and 403. removed.txt is empty. The most any page's words differ from today's is 1.6% (Settings, which gains its bank head).

The console holds on every page. Banks are 4 across on the full lattice, 2 across from 40 to 75rem and 1 on a phone. Each row is as tall as its tallest cell (grid-auto-rows auto, no longer 1fr). Hatched, dashed blank plates close any unfilled row: Home's banks, the Ideas cards, To do's cells, the Plans list, Status's lamp panels and Settings' three-across keys, plus the settings grid on General at 2 across. A cell whose fold is opened takes the whole row, a key opening into a drawer.

Every page has a bank head in Martian Mono caps, with a trail in its bank's colour and a lit square node where the spine turns in. Ideas has '12 IDEAS' in lilac. To do has 'OPEN · 4 SHOWN' in wheat, with 'up to 100' as its quiet link. On Plans, 'SEPTEMBER 2026' is a plans-blue head with Earlier and Later as its links, so it no longer competes with the PLANS title plate. Settings has 'EVERY PART · 9' in steel. The spine also plugs into Status's framed panels at their edge, the settings nav, the new-idea form, each kid on the wishes page and the Plans list.

The spine is one trail: from the title's own line (or her screen on Home) down the gutter, clipped at the foot of main, then carried on by the foot to a node on the horizon. It shows at 78rem and wider. It is hidden on sign-in, the 404 and pages without a title plate.

The foot is where the twist lands. The words come first, on main's own column (mark and legal at x=64, tagline ending at 1215, the cells' edges). Under them is the horizon, and under that the perspective floor, drawn at the lattice's pitch and pivoted on its top edge. Measured, the column guides at x=60/157/253... meet the floor lines exactly at the horizon and fan out below. The foot fills the ground below the horizon, so the straight guides stop there. The page ground keeps only the vertical column guides; the horizontal lattice lines are gone, so sign-in is no longer graph paper.

One phosphor fill per view. On Ideas and To do, Filter is a steel-outline key at the end of the Search cell and lights green on hover and focus. The search box takes the freed cell. ADD AN IDEA is the only green key on Ideas; To do has none until you open the add fold.

One level of cells in forms. The new-idea form and General's groups lose their frame and become banks: each field is a cell with a corner mark, and its outline lights with the box while you write. A form inside a cell (the add-task fold, Save a thought, a folded settings group) is set flat, label over box.

Legibility. The phone tab bar and General's Save bar are solid, with a lit trail along their top edge instead of glass. The tab labels stay at 0.72rem (the 11.5px floor) at 104% width with 0.03em tracking, so WISHES has room inside its key.

Chat. Her message cells are edged in phosphor over a breath of her glass. The family's are edged in amber over a warm grey. The said-by row sets her name in screen green with the layered halo, family names in amber and the time in steel. On desktop the speaker's cell is a 4rem square key. Below 40rem each line takes the full width, with a 1.5rem speaker key in the said-by row.

The light is back where the machine speaks. Home's E7 is back in Grid terms: a bloom of the phosphor rising from under the box's lower left onto the floor, through 3px scanlines. The tubes keep E12-E17: case spill and a breathing power light, glass, the three-layer bloom, the 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen and falloff, inverse plates, block cursors, power-on from opacity 0.05, and the radar's sweep, afterglow, blips and ping. The tube floors, E1 on 'mind', E2 on the mark, E3 on the primary key, E4, E5 focus, E19 her screen and E20 lamps are all kept. screenGlow and glow stay at 1.

Typesetting. Archivo Expanded at 125% in capitals is kept for title plates only. A record's own name (an idea's page, an edit) now uses the 112.5% cut at weight 500, in its own case. Martian Mono is for bank heads (ink) and the label tier (steel), one step below. Archivo is for reading, with tabular lining figures for counts, so the kids' '0 open' is no longer a slashed Ø. The foot is where the twist should land, and it is the weakest seam. Draw the floor at `calc(50% + var(--pitch)/2) 0 / var(--pitch) 100%`: its transform origin is the top edge, so each column guide then runs straight into its floor line at the horizon, which makes 'drawn at exactly that pitch' literally true. firstDraft.name: Grid Console
firstDraft.concept: Every page is a console laid on a twelve-column lattice, and the page floor's grid is drawn at exactly that pitch. The family's things sit in banks of equal cells, like keys on a panel: a plan, a thing to do, an idea, a status lamp, a setting, a day of the month. Rows a bank doesn't fill are closed with hatched blank plates, so the grid always reads as whole. The Tron idea shows in three ways. Cells are drawn by their outlines, which light up and fade like phosphor. The rules are light trails, with a trail spine that runs from each title down the gutter and turns into every bank. The console stands on a perspective Grid floor that runs to a horizon at the foot of every page. The original tube is kept whole: bloom, blur, scanlines, sweep and blips. It's calm, exact and dark, with the green phosphor only where the machine speaks.

designs.name: Folio Switchboard
designs.tagline: The videotex switchboard typeset as its own contents page: titles and heads in Fraunces, and the pictures are the family's own facts printed large, on five steps and in two inks (a count at the end of each leader, how far an idea is by road, the day a thing is due, the days of the month, each person's initial, and each page's folio, the largest and the quietest), while only the machine gives off light.
designs.concept: The parent's switchboard is kept whole: a rack of equal cells, a sommaire Home, numbered pages, and a green tube under every plate. It is typeset as the contents page it always was. Titles and cell heads are in Fraunces, and the page's pictures are the family's own facts printed large: drive times, due days, days of the month, counts, initials. It should feel like an almanac printed on a graphite panel. Everything the family keeps is matte ink at one value. Only the machine gives off phosphor light: the tubes, the radar, her screen, the mark, SEND, the lamps and focus.
designs.companions:
Every companion now has one job, and the job is the same on every page: printing a figure in the hue of what it belongs to. Each figure is printed at one value (oklch L 0.68) with its chroma kept. Colours by owner:
- **Brass #e3cd88:** the service's own pages (Home, Vera, Status, Settings, Family, Memory). It colours their folios, head counts, the settings part digits, the admin's initial, and the accent links.
- **Heather #bc97e8:** Ideas (300).
- **Cornflower #9ccdf8:** Plans (400). It colours the plan leaves, and a faint tint of it marks the empty weekend days on the month.
- **Sea #83d5d4:** To do (500) and its due leaves.
- **Rose #eda6c1:** Wishes (600) and the kids' initials.
- **Ochre #eaa76b:** grown-ups' initials, setup step numbers, a settings part that wants a look, today's leaf and month tile, and 'was due'. It is also the hook for overdue leaves.
- **Kind colours:** each one colours its idea's drive figure. Olive #8d9a5c keeps 'outing' off the brand green.

Each folio is printed a value lower (L 0.55) in its section's hue. Bone #eceee8 is for headings and for the days on the month that hold a plan. Calm green #92dfa7 is for ticks, the box being typed in, and now the lit keycaps. Bright #6dff9c stays where the machine is: tubes with the full kit, the radar and blips, her screens, the mark and caret, primary keys, focus and live lamps.
decisions: Display face (the roll): Fraunces (SOFT 30, WONK 0, optical sizing auto) for h1, h2, cell heads, summaries, month titles, card names and person names. Plex Sans is for reading, Plex Mono for the machine's labels, and VT323 for the glass. A serif makes the parent's contents-page structure (sommaire, leaders, page numbers) literal.

Figures as the pictures (the roll): each is a fact set in Fraunces light, aria-hidden, with the words beside it saying the same thing. They are the drive time on each idea card, calendar leaves for due days and plans, counts ending every contents line, the month's day numbers, initials as monograms, settings part numbers and Status's cost row.

One figure system, written into the sheet. There are five steps on the sqrt-2 ratio of a sheet of paper: 24, 34, 48, 68 and 96px (--f-xs to --f-xl). Each figure takes the step of its job:
- xs (24px): a day in a list, and the kids' keys in the chat.
- s (34px): contents-line counts, Home's leaves, initials beside a name, list steps, month days.
- m (48px): a cell's own figure (drive time, due leaf, plan leaf, settings part, setup step, chat monogram).
- l (68px): a figure that is the cell's whole picture (Status's cost row, a person's own cell).
- xl (96px): the folio only.

Two inks and only two, declared once on every element so each element resolves its own --k or --sec. --fig-ink is oklch(from owner 0.68 c*0.92 h) and --folio-ink is oklch(from sec 0.55 c*0.72 h). I used relative colour rather than the suggested oklch colour-mix. Mixing towards the green-tinted graphite in oklch pulls the hues: heather turned towards blue and rose towards salmon. A fixed value keeps each hue exact and its chroma, so outing's olive is no longer murky. It also makes a row of figures in different colours read as one set of inks. With prefers-contrast: more, both inks switch to full colour.

Lit means the machine, printed means the family. Fraunces is never lit. The ways-to-start keycaps are now VT323 in the calm green with their sunken well and glow. The rule is written into the sheet's header.

The phosphor stays at full strength where the machine is, unchanged from the parent: Home's tube with bloom, blur, scanlines, the lit key word, the radar sweep and blips; the green readout under every plate; the 404 scope; the sign-in face; the mark and cursor; SEND and ADD AN IDEA with their halo; the breathing lamps. glow, screenGlow and topGlow are all 1.0.

Both are off the scale, and the quote is decoration, not a fact. Fix: bring Restaurants to `--f-l` at most, or put its count back at the end of its head like every other cell (`.food-cell .cell-head .count { display: inline }`) and leave the body as the 'Something to eat' line and key. Remove the Memory glyph, or make it a `--f-m` in the same ink. Then Home has one rule: counts at `--f-s` at the end of the leaders, and nothing printed above `--f-m` outside the tube.

Make the figures one system of ink and steps. Today there are six mixes: folio 88% sec with ink, head counts 85% with ink, `.figure` 82% with surface, `.figure-art` 80% with surface, `.initial` 82%, the glyph 40%. There are also a dozen sizes off the declared four steps: keycaps 1.55rem, `.chip-day` 1.7rem, month days 2rem, 2.5rem at line 1345, `.initial` 2.75rem, `.task > .leaf .fig` 3rem, `.setup-list .number` 3.25rem, 9rem and 16rem. Fix: define `--fig-ink: color-mix(in oklch, var(--k, var(--sec)) 72%, var(--surface))` and use it everywhere. Mixing in oklch keeps the hue's chroma, so outing's olive '2ʰ10' and '1ʰ40' stop reading as murky grey-olive. Add `--f-xs: 1.75rem` for keycaps, the chip and month days, and map initials, leaves and setup numbers onto `--f-s` or `--f-m`, so the comment's 'ratio of about 1.5 between steps' is true.

Fraunces should never glow. The Ways to start keycaps (`.starters .key-no`) are Fraunces numerals in `--lit` with a green `text-shadow`. They are the one place a printed face is lit, which blurs the design's clearest rule: the machine speaks VT323 or Plex Mono, and the family's figures are ink. Set `.key-no` in `var(--tube)` at about 1.7rem, keeping the sunken key and its glow. Then 'lit means machine face, printed means Fraunces' holds on every page, and the rule can be written into the standard.

Use one date picture everywhere. Home's Coming up uses the boxed `chip` tile ('OCT' over '1' in a cornflower box), To do uses the unboxed leaf, and the month uses a lone numeral. Put `chip_figure` (the leaf) in Home's `.map .agenda` rows at `--f-xs`/`--f-s`. Let `.map .agenda .what` wrap to two lines instead of `nowrap`/ellipsis, which currently cuts 'Mount St. Helens da…'. On Plans (month), give the days that hold a plan the heading ink and print the empty days in `--dim` (`table.month td:not(:has(.event)) time`), so the eye finds plans rather than 35 equal numerals. On To do, the overdue leaves (27 SEP, 28 SEP) are the same sea as 1 OCT, while Home says 'was due 2 days ago' in ochre. Pass `late` from `views.task_row`, a one-line view change, and set `.leaf.late { --k: var(--people) }`.

Home's tube has a band of dead glass about 170px tall. In home.png, from 'the 4 more on the radar' line (about y 345) down to the dashed rule (about y 515), there is nothing, because `.prompt` is pushed to the foot of `.minitel .crt-tube`. Let the typing area fill the glass instead: `.minitel .prompt { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column }`, `.minitel .prompt-line { flex: 1 }`, `.minitel .prompt-line textarea { flex: 1 }`. The rule and 'What's on your mind?' then sit right under Next up, and the empty glass becomes the page you type on, which is what a terminal's screen is. Alternatively, grow `.next-up .radar` to fill the band.

On Ideas, say each fact once and make the fallback safe. A macro returns its markup, so a card can do `{% set fig = drive_figure(idea.away, 'card-art') %}{% if fig | trim %}{{ fig }}{{ idea.away }}{% else %}` followed by the visible words. When the figure draws, the sentence 'about 2 h 10 min south of home (estimate)' stops showing twice. When `views.drive_text` is reworded and the parse fails, the words come back instead of nothing. Keep 'about' and '(estimate)' visible as a small '≈' before `.drive .fig`. Status's cost sentence can stay, since it adds 'at a tenth of the price'.

Controls and the phone. On General, the time-zone select wraps 'Default (Vancouver · UTC-07:00)' onto two lines, making a 66px key beside 46px fields. Add `select { white-space: nowrap }` and `select > button, select selectedcontent { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis }`. On chat-phone, the deck on one row clips 'who is asking?' and hides 'Send where I am' behind a bare checkbox and crosshair (`.page-chat .deck .locate-words` is visually hidden). Wrap it as Home's phone deck does: `.page-chat .deck { flex-wrap: wrap }`, `.page-chat .deck .locate { order: 5; flex: 1 1 100% }`, and drop the `.locate-words` hiding.

firstDraft.name: Folio Switchboard
firstDraft.concept: The parent's switchboard, with its rack of equal cells, its sommaire Home, its numbered pages and a green tube under every plate, is now typeset like the contents page it always claimed to be. Page titles and cell heads are in Fraunces, a display serif with optical sizes. The pictures are no longer mosaic icons: they are the page's own facts, set large in Fraunces light. The effect is an almanac printed on a graphite panel: the family's figures are printed in grounded colour, and only the machine gives off phosphor light.

designs.name: Desk Terminal, Joined
designs.tagline: Desk Terminal made whole: every page opens on one head row, the terminal beside the desk fits, sticks or folds to a line, Home's question is its headline typed at the foot of the glass with the box as the tube's last rows, and the light reaches the desk and Status as data.
designs.concept: One real terminal still stands at the left of the family's desk, the only cased, rounded, lit thing on the page, but now it joins the page instead of crowding it. On Home it reads like a real terminal: scrollback at the top of the glass (her screen, the day, Next up in inverse, the radar), her question at its foot as the page's 40px headline, and the box to answer in as the tube's last rows, over a graphite keyboard ledge. Everywhere else a head row names the page first, and the terminal fits the screen and sticks, or folds to one lit line where nothing is live. The phosphor now carries data on the desk too: a white-hot NOW lamp with a lit stretch of rail, a steady lit NOW tick in To do, and a moving-coil spend meter on Status. The feel is a calm, grounded desk with one live machine on it.
designs.companions: Steel reverse (--rev #6b8396, cap --rev-cap #9cc4dc) for 'here', the latched key, the band rings, the rails and the afterglow's 12% wash. Denim (#9db6d6) for links only, so month abbreviations are now bone. Sage (#86d9a6) for lit states, the LED on a latched key and the afterglow's edge. A cobalt wash (#4f60e6 at 2.2) sits at the terminal's top right. Graphite is used for the machine's body, bezel and keyboard ledge, and slate trays for the desk. Amber appears only as words, rings and the late bar on the glass. Each kind keeps its own colour, named in words mixed 72% toward the ink, and the bar's section icons are mixed 60% toward the ink. #6dff9c is kept for the mark, Send and the page's primary, 'mind', focus, the lamps, the tubes, the NOW run and tick, and the needle.
decisions: Built as a clean sheet with build.py, the parent's method: today's themed stylesheet with sizes moved onto the steps, then palette.css. The steps are 12/15/17/22/32/44, and the glass has its own 20/28/40. Sheet: 195,958 of 200,000 characters. The Home Contents rules and the Home view timelines were cut to make room.

HOME, the question is the headline again (skeptic, type, style, usability, feedback, soul). The terminal is 33rem wide beside a 1fr desk. The glass top holds her screen and 'VERA · TUE 29 SEP' dim, then NEXT UP in inverse with a 7.25rem radar. At the glass foot the question is set in VT323 40px with a straight U+0027 apostrophe, 'mind' at a #e4fff0 core with E1's two halos, and a block cursor that blinks 8 times and then stays lit. The question is still the textarea's <label>.

The box joins the glass (soul, style, feedback). The _ask form now wraps the tube, because ask.js looks for the textarea inside form.ask. The textarea is a glass-tinted well under the prompt: color-mix(screen 6%, #050806), a 1px phosphor-dim edge, 3 rows, bone Plex 17px, a green caret, a faint resting halo and E4 on focus. It sits on the glass, above the scanlines, and is not blurred.

The keyboard ledge (usability, style). It is graphite with a 1px dark engraved lip and a 6% top highlight, and E7's pool rises from under Send. From, the mic and Send share one row. Send has one 2px focus ring and keeps its pool. 'Send where I am' sits under the row. The three ways to start are one row of 15px keys that does not wrap on desktop. The Home terminal is 646px, ends at 733px and is sticky. The Tab order is Pho Oregon, '4 plans on the radar', textarea, From, mic, Send, the checkbox, then the starters.

A HEAD ROW on every inner page (interaction, type, skeptic). page_head hands its head to the frame, so base.html draws it first, across terminal and desk: the icon, an h1 in Plex Sans Condensed 600 at 44px on one line, a balanced lede, and the one green key at the right. The keys are Add an idea, Add something to do, and Put something on the calendar where a calendar is connected. On To do and Plans the key targets the add form, which is folded out of sight until asked for, so the words appear once. The DOM order is head row, terminal, desk. This also fixed a grid bug: a spanning head sized its row as if it had wrapped, so the terminal and desk now sit in their own grid (.bench).

The TERMINAL fits, sticks or folds (system, usability, interaction, skeptic). It is sticky at bar + 1rem with max-height 100dvh - bar - 2rem, and no terminal overflows at 1280×900: Ideas ends at 858, Status 878, To do 681, the month 646, General 825 and Chat 551. On Ideas, Kind is the only open bank, three up with icon and word, and For and Status fold behind one key that states the filter, 'For anyone · any but dropped' (Single Quote's chip). Pages with nothing live fold: the form, an idea's edit, Wishes, Family, Memory, Your password and the Settings overview. Folding is decided in base.html from empty tube, deck and Contents blocks, so pages that are not copied fold as well. There the terminal becomes one cased strip under the head (lamp · Ready · who answers · spend · Status →) and the desk takes a 62rem measure. The Settings bank appears only on section pages.

CONTENTS only where it is a contents (usability, interaction, skeptic). Status keeps its 8-part plate with leaders and the in-view latch. Home's plate is gone: its counts moved to the band heads, and the numbered rings stay as the page's pagination, with setup's in amber. Chat's plate lists the conversations, 'Family · Maya · Theo', as numbered 44px stops, with the open one latched in steel.

LIGHT AS DATA on the desk (feedback, soul; grafted from Traced). Band heads show a tabular figure over a caps label before the see-more link: '4 / PLANS', '4 OPEN · 2 late' and '12 / IDEAS'. '2 late' is an amber link to /tasks?when=late, and the links now read 'Things to do' and 'All ideas' so nothing repeats the figure. The NOW lamp is white-hot and breathes, and it is the only breathing lamp on Home (the foot lamp is steady there). A 2px lit stretch with the two-layer halo runs from it and fades to steel before the first stop; it samples (108,255,155) at 1x. On Home and To do a steady lit NOW tick sits between the late rows and the rest, a steel rail threads the tick wells, and a short lit run leads down to the next well.

The To do tube's rows are links (usability). Late, This week, Later and No date each link to ?when=…, and the one showing turns inverse on the glass (amber for Late). The late flag and the filter are computed in the template, as in Traced's template; the shipped view would take `when` and hand each row `late`.

STATUS's tube is a panel meter (feedback, soul; grafted from Metered, with its judges' fixes). The scale runs from 0 to 125% of the limit, labelled only 0, 1.00 and 2.00. The limit is a lit long tick with the overrun hatched past it. The needle has a #e4fff0 core, a halo and a white tip, and kicks once as the tube warms. There are no number wheels. The figure '$0.00 TODAY' is on the glass above the scale, with '0% of limit' beside it. A ghost needle at 30% opacity rests on 'Average day $0.04' (explained under weaknesses). The foot says '$0.00 of $2.00 today' in words and does not link to Status from Status.

CHAT (soul, style). Her glyph screen is 6rem with E19's fall, once as the page opens and continuously while she thinks. The foot (READY lamp, who answers, spend, Status) sits beside the screen instead of repeating it, and the conversations plate comes after. The thread stays on the steel track and ends in the lit ring at the composer. On a phone the composer is pinned above the tab bar at 200px at most, and the plate is kept there.

THE AFTERGLOW, visible and never a selection (every lens). It only happens under (hover:hover). The row takes a 12% #9cc4dc wash in .12s, and a separate layer draws a 2px sage edge with a 0 0 18px -10px sage halo while the leader is traced in sage. Chromium does not transition out of a CSS animation, which is why the edge used to snap off, so the rest decay is itself a transition: the layer is lit by `opacity` and decays at rest through `filter: opacity()` (0.9s after 0.3s). On leave, opacity fades over 1.2s and the filter snaps back only after 1.2s. The motion-glow frames sample the edge at (71,109,93), (47,71,65), (25,38,37), then back to surface, with the wash (34,45,50) → (18,24,27). A parked pointer shows the wash alone. The rails moved into the tick cell's pseudo-elements to free the row's own for the afterglow. It is never amber, and setup rows use the same steel wash.

Small fixes. Months are bone (type, skeptic). Ideas has separate DRIVE and WAY columns (type). The pencil became 'Edit or snooze' in words at the row's end, regular weight in ink-2, underlined on hover (usability). Column heads sit on the same grid as their rows, so WHO, DUE, DRIVE, WAY, FOR and # line up exactly. The case has an 8px outer radius, a 5px face and a 1px engraved rim; the glass keeps its rounder 12/14px curve, with the 14px chin, vents, LED and 80px spill (feedback, owner). Bar icons are mixed 60% toward the ink (feedback). The separator dot sits outside the late link so it is not underlined.

PHONE (system, usability). No CSS order is used anywhere: build.py removes the one `order: 3` the base sheet had and asserts that none is left. Home is the terminal first (glass with Next up, question and well, then ledge, then foot), then the desk. Other pages go head row, a designed compact tube of 118-162px (nearest and furthest lines, the trace's extra line and the tally's last line hidden; a smaller dial), one Filter key holding the banks, the foot line, then the desk. To do rows go to two lines on a phone, the title, then the due words beside 'Edit or snooze'.

KEPT from the parent: every token and glow number (all 1.0, wash 2.2), --shadow 0 0 #0000, flat graphite keys with the steel latched key and its sage LED, the Ready foot, one-line desk rows with leaders only before facts, WHO · DUE heads, amber 'was due' words and amber ring wells, denim underlined sentence-case links, words in the bar, the one-screen month with shaded weekends and today in steel, and the 404 and sign-in terminals. Added only --rev and --rev-cap as the brief asked (with --steel aliasing them), plus --hot, --sage, --wash and --rail-glow.

Words changed, measured at 20.2% at worst on To do: 'Edit or snooze', 'Now', 'Things to do' and 'All ideas' as head links, 'Average day', and the Ideas fold summary. Removed items are listed in removed.txt: Home's Contents plate, the Settings overview bank, and the terminal column on pages with nothing live. For and Status on Ideas are folded, not removed.

One head row on every inner page, with icon, 44px condensed title, lede and the one green key, gives title → action → machine → rows in both the sight line and the DOM. Pages with nothing live fold to one cased strip, so there are no empty graphite columns.
Every terminal fits 900px without an inner scroll bar. Ideas keeps Kind as the only open bank (three up), with For and Status behind a key that states the filter.

Light now carries data on the desk and on Status: the white-hot NOW lamp with a lit 2px run, the steady NOW tick threading To do's wells, the To do tube rows as links that go inverse when chosen, and a moving-coil meter whose needle kicks on warm-up.
The afterglow is finally visible and decays correctly, both at rest and on leave. It was rebuilt as transition-only layers after a test showed Chromium will not transition out of an animation.
Column heads share their rows' grids, so the fact columns align exactly. Drive and way are split, months are bone, denim marks links only, and the edit control is words, not a pencil.
0 small targets and no sideways scroll on every page. There is no CSS order anywhere, enforced in the build, and the Tab order matches the drawing on desktop and phone.

The head row costs about 100-110px on every inner page. Status's terminal ends at 878px, just inside the fold, and Chat's thread starts lower than in the parent.

The page head is hoisted to the frame through flask `g` (page_head stores it and base.html draws it first). This keeps every page's head in the head row without copying templates, but the shipped app should make it a block. The `when` filter and the late flag are computed in the template, so the view would need to take them.

The To do and Plans add forms stay hidden until the head row's key targets them, using :target and ::details-content. A browser without ::details-content shows the closed fold with its summary instead, which still works but is less direct.
The Coming up figure says '4 plans' although five are coming; the fifth is Next up on the glass. This matches the glass's '4 plans on the radar' but can read as an off-by-one.
Phone tubes are compact at 118-162px, which leaves the dial's numerals and the trace's day numbers small (they are aria-hidden).
The sheet is at 195.9k of the 200k budget, so there is little room for the next round's additions without trimming the base.
Chat shows her name in the bar and in the head row, and her screen in the terminal as well as beside each of her lines. That is a lot of Vera on one screen, though each has a job.

designs.name: Backlit Plate
designs.tagline: One live phosphor screen lies behind the whole page and a matte slate plate is laid over it: light shows only where the plate is cut, and the plate is cut only where the machine is live.
designs.concept: The page is a backlit faceplate: one continuous, square, matte slate plate is laid over a live phosphor screen and centred on the black room. Every light the original tube gave off is still there at full strength, but each has a physical cause. "mind" is stencilled through the plate, Send is a backlit key whose light pools out of its gap, a field's cut edge lights while you type, every lamp is a pinhole, and the screens are windows whose light falls on their bevels and spills onto the plate. The shape of a cut says what it shows: a slot is time, a round window is place, a square window is Vera, and a 4:3 window is the screen proper. Where nothing is live the plate stays whole, so the page feels calm and material, and the green appears only where attention belongs.
designs.companions: Cool slate #13181b is the plate itself. Graphite #192024, with an engraved edge and a 5% top light, is every plate key. Steel reverse (#6b8396, a #9cc4dc cap and a lit pinhole LED) marks 'here' and the latched key: in the bar, the phone's tab bar, the Ideas kinds, the To do show-keys, Plans List/Month, the Settings list and today on the month. Steel #82a4b5 is the accent of the pages with no colour of their own. Denim #9db6d6, underlined, is for links. Pewter #47535b leads every engraved rule. Bone ink #d4cfc4 is the reading text and linen #ebe6da the heads, with #a9b3bb for the engraved caps legends. Square steel bubbles with the steel cap carry the family's chat lines, and dark glass #0c110e carries Vera's. Amber appears only as words, rings and one rule lead, for late and for needs-a-look. Each kind is named in its own colour mixed 72% toward the ink, and its row icon takes the same colour. The green stays in the cuts: #6dff9c on the mark, the backlit key, 'mind', focus, the pinholes, the windows and their bevels; lit sage #86d9a6 on ticks and the row afterglow's edge.
decisions: Built as a clean sheet with Desk Terminal's build.py method (variants/r13-idea-2/build.py). The harness themes today's stylesheet for these tokens, so E1-E22 are all present at glow, screenGlow and topGlow 1.0. Every font size off the glass is then rewritten in place onto six steps (12/15/17/22/30/44), with the glass's own VT323 sizes left alone, and the design's own rules (plate.css, 64k) follow. Sheet: 170,785 characters of 200k.
THE RULE is written at the head of plate.css. washGlow is 0 because a coloured corner would be light with no cut. --shadow is 0 0 #0000, never none.

No monitor cases anywhere. .crt became the cut: a transparent 6px chamfer, a 1px dark engraved edge with a light lip, the tube's light on the bevel (a 42% phosphor-on-plate ring plus a 6px, 30% bloom; it samples (57,121,81) at 100%), and E12's 80px spill offset onto the plate below. Vents and a pinhole power LED sit under Home's Next up and under sign-in only.

Shapes as a system, one macro each in _ui.html: slot() and plan_slot() for time, a round window for the Ideas radar, presence squares with lit bevels for Vera, 4:3 windows for Next up, spend, sign-in and 404, and pin() for lamps. Slots are on Home's Coming up, the Plans list and month, and To do (-14 … NOW … +14 with amber late ticks and '2 LATE' as a link on the glass). Slot positions use generated .at-N classes, so there is no inline style.

I bent the sweep: it is a hot 3px trace with an afterglow tail drawn along the slot's axis. It sits under the next plan's label and above the numerals, so it never crosses a word. A plan today becomes a hot head on the breathing NOW line instead of a second mark beside it.

I bent the month slot. The month view hands the template only the weeks it draws, so on Plans/month the slot is that month as time, with NOW lit where it falls and past days dimmed, not NOW at the left edge. Home and the Plans list keep the four weeks from now.

Engraved rules replace every panel and tray. A 3px pewter lead over the icon column, the title in the break (Instrument Sans wdth 75/600 at 22px), and a groove (1px #0a0d0e over a 1px #283036 lip) run to the figure and its way on. Rule figures set the numeral in Plex Mono and the word in the sans, so there is no mono sentence. Pages that keep today's markup get the same rule from .panel > h2 and details folds, so Settings, Family, Memory and Wishes follow it with no markup change.

Rows are printed on the plate: an icon column, the title, a dotted leader, and fixed tabular facts in per-list --cols, with engraved caps column heads (DAY·AT·IN, WHO·DUE, DRIVE·WAY·FOR·#, FOR·#). I found and freed a base .lead rule (60ch, a bottom margin) that had been cutting the leaders short.

Row afterglow: a 12% steel wash with a 2px sage edge. It uses its own slower 1.2s curve (--row-fade) so it is still visible at 380ms in motion-glow, where the kit's fast-falling afterglow curve had it gone.

Home is a 7fr/5fr greeting. On the left: Vera's square window and 'Vera · Tue 29 Sep', the 44px question with 'mind' stencilled (E1), a 3-row well with a resting halo, From, mic and Send on one row, and Send where I am under them. I reordered the markup rather than using CSS order, so Tab follows the drawing. The E7 pool with masked scanlines spills from under the well and Send (1px under Send is (42,86,61)). On the right, Next up fills a 4:3 window and warms up from one line: its contents are wrapped so the picture opens as a whole. The dashboard is two stacks: Coming up and Lately added, beside To do, the kids' wishes and Something to eat. Home is 1701px at 1280.

Ideas: head row, then Search with its key and a For/Status fold, with the 8rem round window and a one-line nearest/furthest readout beside them ('18 min NW' unbroken). The kind keys run as one row under both, and 8 rows show above the fold. I dropped the Kind select and the Restaurants tab: Restaurant is a key. 'Save a thought for later' moved below the list.

Status: the 4:3 spend screen sits at the head's right, with the figure in words in the lede. Sections are one-line pinhole rows (on lit, off a dark hole ringed red, part half amber) with leaders, capped at 62rem. Only the Ready pinhole breathes.
Chat: the thread is printed on the plate. The family's lines are square steel with the cap; Vera's are dark-glass windows. Only her newest window's bevel is lit; older bevels are dark (decayed).

Type uses three faces: Instrument Sans across its width axis (75/600 heads, 430 reading, 520 row titles), IBM Plex Mono for figures only (tabular, slashed zero), and VT323 only on glass. The legal footer moved out of mono. There are no tracked caps on controls.

Targets: 0 under 44px on all 13 shots. Inline links reach 44px by zero-specificity padding (:where), so the text does not move. Tick wells are 44px inputs that draw a 1.3rem well via ::after. Mics, crumbs, the bar and the menu are all at least 2.75rem.

Access. More contrast turns off bevels, spills, scanlines and blur and outlines windows in phosphor. Reduced motion stops the trace, the warm-up and breathing, and the marks stay lit. Forced colours outline windows and pinholes, and I fixed a forced-colours checkbox that painted a false tick.

It answers the owner's latest word at the root: the original light is back at full strength, and every effect has a physical cause (a cut, a gap, a pinhole, a stencil), so scarcity is a fact of the object, not a style rule.
