briefs.name: Desk Terminal, Joined
briefs.hypothesis:
REFINEMENT of the strongest carried winner, Desk Terminal (r12-idea-2).

Its record:
- 8.34, in all 8 top fours, 7 promise votes.
- First with feedback, soul, style, system, interaction, usability and the skeptic.
- Its weakest lenses are type (7.5), the skeptic (7.8) and style (8.0).

Its losses are narrow, and each is a template fix, not a flaw in the idea (the machine states, the desk holds):
- Home lost its headline. The question became a small VT323 line with a high curly apostrophe, so Home's largest head is 'Finish setting up' (skeptic, type, style). The box is the smallest of the leaders and reads as a loose form under a tube (usability, style, feedback, soul).
- On inner pages the tube comes before the h1 in the sight line and in the DOM, and 2rem titles lose to it (interaction, type, skeptic).
- The Contents plate repeats the band heads, and Settings lists its pages twice (skeptic, usability, interaction, system).
- The Ideas terminal scrolls inside itself. Pages with nothing live keep an empty column (system, usability, interaction, skeptic, style, soul).
- The row afterglow is invisible for the fourth round (soul, usability).
- Smaller faults: denim months that are not links, drive and way sharing a column, a pencil hiding 'complete, or snooze', CSS order on the phone, a double focus ring on Send, and 'Status →' on Status itself.

The lenses also asked it to grow in two places where the light carries data:
- Traced's lit rail from NOW and its head figures on the desk (feedback);
- Metered's phosphor needle as Status's tube (feedback, soul).

What should happen:
- Type and the skeptic should rise, because the headline and title hierarchy come back.
- Usability and interaction should hold at 8.6-9.0 or rise, because every one of their fixes is applied.
- Feedback and soul should rise, because light now reaches the desk and Status as data, and the typing joins the glass.

Why it should beat the other three carried:
- Traced has no machine layout and a barcode trace.
- Long Persistence's Status tables wrap, and its sweep crosses words.
- Track Diagram Relit has an icon-only bar, no 'was due' words, and is invisible in stills.

It is not this round's graphics mutant of the same parent. That mutant redraws the map and the lamp family and fixes nothing. This child keeps the lamps and fixes the named faults.
briefs.brief:
START FROM Desk Terminal:
- Palette: rounds/r13/palettes/r12-idea-2.json.
- Variant: rounds/r13/variants/r12-idea-2/. It is a clean sheet built by build.py from tokens.json plus palette.css (76k). The sheet is 183k of the 200k budget, so fold repeated rules and drop the Home Contents rules you no longer need.
- Templates: base, home, _ask, _ui, ideas, tasks, plans, plans_month, status, chat, settings, settings_section, login, 404, 403.
- Shots: rounds/r13/out/r12-idea-2/shots/.
- Judging: rounds/r12/results.json under r12-idea-2. Read all eight lenses' fixes.

GRAFT SOURCES
- Traced's head figure over label, the lit stretch of rail from the NOW lamp, the steady NOW tick in To do, and its late filter: rounds/r13/variants/r12-idea-1/templates (tasks.html sets late from today_iso) and the css in rounds/r13/palettes/r12-idea-1.json.
- Metered's panel meter: the spend_dial macro in rounds/r12/variants/r12-mut-2/templates/_ui.html and its css in that variant's palette.css.
- phosphor_kit.md E1, E3, E4, E13-E17, E19 and E20.

KEEP
- The rule: the terminal is the only cased, rounded, lit object; the desk is square, matte slate.
- One tube per page drawing live data, and the warm-up from a bright line (start at .05 opacity).
- Flat graphite keys; the latched key in steel reverse with a lit sage LED.
- The Ready foot, with Contents on long pages.
- One-line desk rows, with a leader only before a fact, fixed tabular sub-columns, and WHO · DUE column heads.
- Amber 'was due' words and amber ring wells.
- Denim underlined sentence-case links, and words in the bar.
- Chat's steel track ending in a lit ring, with the family on the right.
- The one-screen month, with weekends shaded and today in steel.
- 0 targets under 44px.
- Every token and glow number (all 1.0), and `--shadow: 0 0 #0000`.

CHANGE, most-cited first

1) HOME: THE QUESTION IS THE HEADLINE AGAIN, AND THE BOX JOINS THE GLASS (skeptic, usability, system, style, feedback, soul, type)

On Home only, the terminal is 32-34rem wide, beside a 1fr desk with a 2rem gap. Read it like a real terminal: scrollback at the top of the glass, the prompt at its foot, the keyboard under it.

- Glass top:
  - her screen and 'VERA · TUE 29 SEP' at dim strength;
  - then NEXT UP in inverse, the plan, its date and '4 plans on the radar', with the radar (7-7.5rem) at the right;
  - no empty glass.
- Glass foot, the question:
  - VT323 at the 40px step, so it is the largest thing on Home;
  - a straight apostrophe (U+0027 in the template, since VT323's curly one draws high);
  - 'mind' at hot core with E1's two halos;
  - a block cursor that blinks 8 times, then stays lit;
  - it stays the textarea's <label>.
- Directly under the question, still inside the glass frame, the textarea is the tube's last rows:
  - a glass-tinted well (color-mix(in srgb, var(--screen) 6%, #050806)) with a 1px phosphor-dim edge;
  - at least 3 rows, at full glass width;
  - the family's words in IBM Plex Sans 17px bone (#d4cfc4), never VT323 or green, with a green caret;
  - E4 on focus (3px ring and 22px bloom), and the faint halo at rest.
- The deck is a keyboard ledge under the glass: graphite, with a 1px engraved lip and a 6% top highlight.
  - From, the mic and Send sit on one row. Send is the page's one primary, with E3's ring and pool and ONE 2px focus ring with its halo, not two rings.
  - 'Send where I am' sits under that row.
  - The three ways to start are one row of flat 15px graphite keys that does not wrap.
- The whole Home terminal is about 820px or less, so its foot shows at 1280x900, and it is sticky.
- Tab order follows the drawing: the Next up link, the textarea, From, the mic, Send, Send where I am, the ways to start, the foot.
- Keep `.next-up` on the glass.

2) A HEAD ROW ON EVERY INNER PAGE (interaction, type, skeptic)
- It spans terminal and desk:
  - the section icon;
  - an h1 at 2.75rem (44px), Plex Sans Condensed 600, on one line and balanced;
  - the lede;
  - the page's one green primary at the right (Add an idea, Add something to do).
- The terminal and the desk start on one line under it.
- DOM order is head row, then terminal (tube, then deck), then desk, so the eye and the Tab order both go title, action, tube, filters, list.

3) THE TERMINAL FITS, STICKS, OR FOLDS (system, usability, interaction, skeptic, soul, style)
- It is sticky on every page, Home included: top is the bar plus 1rem, max-height is calc(100dvh - bar - 2rem), and there is no inner scroll bar. Design each terminal to fit 900px.
- Ideas:
  - Search, then the Kind bank as the only kind filter: two-up, or three-up as icon plus a short word.
  - For and Status fold into one disclosure whose summary states the filter ('For anyone · any but dropped'). That is Single Quote's filter-summary chip, which interaction asked to graft.
  - The terminal ends at about 860px or less.
- Pages with nothing live (the new-idea form, an idea's edit, Wishes, Family, Memory, Your password) get no column:
  - the status foot becomes a one-line strip under the head row (lamp, who answers, spend, 'Status →');
  - the desk takes the full width at a 62rem measure.
- The Settings overview folds too, because its desk rows already list the parts with their states. The section bank appears only on the section pages, as their nav with one latched key.
- On Status, hide the foot's 'Status →'.

4) CONTENTS ONLY WHERE IT IS A CONTENTS (usability, interaction, skeptic; feedback, style and type keep it)
- Keep it on Status (8 parts) under the tube, with the ring rail, leaders to tabular figures and the in-view latch.
- Drop it from Home (5 bands). Home's counts move to the band heads (see 5), and the numbered steel rings stay on the band heads as the page's pagination, with setup's ring in amber.
- On Chat, the plate becomes the kids' conversations: numbered stops 'Family · Maya · Theo', each a 44px link (style).

5) THE DESK CARRIES LIGHT AS DATA (feedback, soul; Traced's graft)
- Each band head gets Traced's figure over a caps label, before its 'see more' link:
  - '4 / PLANS';
  - '4 OPEN · 2 late', where '2 late' is amber words linking to To do filtered to late;
  - '12 / IDEAS'.
  - No head repeats its rows.
- Coming up's rail:
  - the white-hot NOW lamp breathes, and it is the only breathing lamp on Home;
  - a 2px lit stretch runs from it to the first stop, with the two-layer halo (0 0 4px brand/.8, 0 0 12px brand/.35), fading to steel before the stop;
  - it must be visible at 1x.
- To do, on Home and on its page: a steady lit NOW tick between the late rows and the rest, with the rail threading the tick wells.
- To do's tube: each bar row ('Late 2') is a link to its filter. Ship the views.task_row `late` flag as Traced's template does.

6) STATUS'S TUBE BECOMES A PANEL METER (feedback, soul; Metered, with the fixes its judges asked for)
- The spend tube draws a phosphor moving-coil meter:
  - the scale runs from $0 to 125% of the limit, with the limit marked and the overrun hatched;
  - the needle has a hot #e4fff0 core and a halo, and kicks as the tube warms up.
- A ghost needle at 30% shows the day's peak, or yesterday's reading when today is 0, so $0.00 still reads as a measurement in a still.
- The figure stays on the glass above the scale ('$0.00 TODAY'). No number wheels.
- The foot says it in words: '$0.00 of $2.00 today'.

7) CHAT'S TERMINAL (soul, style)
- Her glyph screen large (E19 at about 6rem, falling once on arrival and while she thinks), then the READY lamp, who answers, and the kids' conversations plate.
- The desk keeps the thread hung on the steel track, ending in the lit ring at the composer at the thread's foot.

8) THE AFTERGLOW, VISIBLE AND NEVER A SELECTION (every lens; open for four rounds)
- Only under (hover:hover). Pointing lights a row in .12s with:
  - a 12% steel wash (#9cc4dc into the row);
  - a 2px sage (#86d9a6) left edge;
  - a 0 0 18px -10px sage halo;
  - its leader traced in sage.
- Leaving fades it over 1.2s ease-out, and motion-glow-1 to 3 must show the decay.
- While the pointer rests, the edge and halo decay to the wash alone within 1.2s, so a parked mouse never reads as a selection.
- Never amber.
- Keep `.idea-card` on the idea rows.

9) SMALL TYPE AND WORD FIXES (type, skeptic, usability, system, feedback)
- Month abbreviations in bone ink, since denim means a link.
- Ideas get two columns, DRIVE ('27 min') and WAY ('S').
- The pencil becomes words at the row's end: 'Edit or snooze', in regular weight and ink-2, underlined on hover.
- The case: 8px outer radius, a 5px face and a 1px engraved rim. The glass keeps its own curvature. Keep the 14px chin with vents and LED, and the 80px spill.
- Bar icons' section tints mixed 60% toward the ink.

10) PHONE (system, usability)
- No CSS order anywhere: the DOM order is the drawing.
- Home: the terminal first (the tube with Next up, then the question and the well, then the ledge), then the desk.
- Other pages:
  - the head row, then a compact tube of 160px or less;
  - then one 'Filter' disclosure holding the banks;
  - then the foot line;
  - then the desk.
- The Chat composer is pinned above the tab bar, 200px at most.

TOKENS: as r12-idea-2, unchanged. In css: --rev #6b8396 and --rev-cap #9cc4dc.

REMOVED (write removed.txt): Home's Contents plate (its counts moved to the band heads); the Settings overview bank (it listed the pages twice); the terminal column on pages with nothing live (folded to a foot strip). For and Status on Ideas are folded, not removed.

CHECK
- 0 targets under 44px on every page.
- Tab order matches the drawing on desktop and phone.
- Home's terminal foot is inside 900px, and the Ideas terminal has no inner scroll.
- A green ring on every control, open selects and checkboxes included.
- The details strip finds .idea-card, .next-up, #title, .field.wide, label.check and details.menu > summary.
- The afterglow decays in motion-glow.

briefs.name: Backlit Plate
briefs.brief:
BUILD
Either:
- a main-lane palette (so every kit effect is inherited) with its own templates and up to 60k of css; or
- if the budget binds, a clean sheet made by Desk Terminal's build.py method: today's themed sheet so E1-E22 are all present, plus your own rules.

Start the templates from today's (/home/user/FamilyDB/src/familydb/web/templates).

Read, for ideas only:
- Glow Ink Zine: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-1, how its templates open the page over the tube. Take the hole and nothing else: no tears, tape, kraft, ransom letters, red marker or one-size type.
- Front Panel: rounds/r5/palettes/r5-idea-2.json, its legends set into the rules.
- Bench Scope: rounds/r10/variants/r10-wild-2/templates/_ui.html, its civil() and trace() macros.
- phosphor_kit.md, whole.

THE RULE (write it at the head of the css): 'One screen, one plate. Nothing on the page glows by itself; light shows only where the plate is cut, and the plate is cut only where the machine is live.'

THE PLATE
- Each page is ONE continuous square plate of matte slate (surface #13181b), max about 76rem, centred on the black room (bg #0b0e0c).
  - At least 2rem of black shows at each side on desktop, and 8px on the phone.
  - It has a 1px engraved outer edge and E8's 4% top-edge highlight.
  - No trays, cards or bands inside it, no texture, no screws.
- Parts of a page are divided by ENGRAVED RULES:
  - a 3px pewter lead (#47535b) about 2.75rem long, over the icon column, then a hairline groove (1px #0a0d0e with a 1px #283036 lip under it) to the plate's edge;
  - the section title set IN the rule's break (Front Panel's legend in the frame line, as feedback asked of Metered);
  - the head's figure and its 'see more' link at the rule's right end.
- The family's rows are printed on the plate: one line each, with a leader only before a fact, a fixed tabular facts column, and column heads (WHO · DUE, DRIVE · WAY · FOR · #) as engraved caps legends.

THE CUTS, one vocabulary on every page

1) WINDOWS: rounded like a CRT's glass (about 14px/16px), cut to their content, never empty.
- Inside: E13-E17 at full. VT323 (1.5rem, never under 1.2) with three halos and a .35px blur; scanlines 1 in 3 at 40%; the sheen; the 60% falloff; sweep, blips and pings.
- The bevel: a 5-6px chamfer round the glass, lit by the screen. It runs from color-mix(in srgb, var(--screen) 30%, var(--surface)) at the glass edge to the plate at its outer edge, clearly visible at 100%.
- The spill: E12's 80px phosphor spill falls onto the plate below the window.
- Under the Home and sign-in windows only, a row of engraved vent slots and a pinhole power LED in the plate. That is all that is left of the case.
- Warm-up from a bright line (E16, starting at .05 opacity) on sign-in, 404 and Home's Next up.

2) THE SHAPE SAYS WHAT IT SHOWS
- A SLOT (a long window about 64px tall, across its section) is TIME.
  - Four weeks on a dial scale, with day ticks and week numerals at 15px under the axis.
  - NOW is lit hot at the left edge. A lit mark sits at each plan day, 70% of the slot tall, with a 2px hot core.
  - The next plan is labelled on the glass ('THU 1').
  - A 1px sweep runs under the labels only, never across a word.
  - Used on Home's Coming up and the Plans list and month. On To do it runs -14 … NOW … +14, with a tick keyed to each dated task and '2 LATE' in amber on the glass as a link to the late filter.
- A ROUND window is PLACE: the radar (E17), on Ideas beside the filters at 8rem with its nearest and furthest readout (one line each; keep '[18 MIN NW]' unbroken), and on an idea's page with its own blip.
- A SQUARE window is VERA: her glyph screen (E19), beside her name on Home, large at the head of Chat, and as each of her lines' mark.
- A 4:3 window is the SCREEN proper: Home's Next up, Status's spend (the original's own spend screen: '$0.00' big, '[........] 0%', 'OF THE $2.00 DAILY LIMIT'), sign-in's face (E22) and the 404 flicker (E18).

3) PINHOLES: every lamp is a 7-8px hole through the plate.
- On: #6dff9c with E20's two-layer halo.
- Off: a dark hole with a 1.5px red ring.
- Part: half amber.
- Only the live one breathes: NOW on Home, Ready on the other pages.
- Used for Status's rows (the annunciator is rows with a pinhole each, never tiles), the NOW tick between late and upcoming on To do, Ready in each page head, and the LED beside a latched key.

4) STENCIL: the word 'mind' in Home's question is cut through the plate. It is #6dff9c with E1's two halos, the one lit word on the page.

5) BACKLIT KEY: the page's one primary (Send, Add an idea, Add it) is a translucent key over the light: #6dff9c, with E3's 1px ring and the light pooling 8px out of its gap onto the plate, brighter on hover and fading over 1.2s. Every other key is a flat plate key: graphite #192024, a 1px engraved edge, a 5% top highlight, sentence case.

6) WELLS: fields and tick wells are cuts onto dark glass (field #070b09) with a 1.5px #5b6570 lip, so they still read as boxes.
- A field's text is the reading face in bone, with a green caret.
- On focus its cut edge lights (E4: a 3px ring and a 22px bloom), fading over 1.2s.
- A ticked well shows lit sage (#86d9a6) light through the tick.
- Home's ask well keeps a faint resting halo, and the E7 pool with its masked scanlines spills onto the plate from under Send and the well.

WHERE THE PLATE IS CUT, page by page
- Home, a 7fr/5fr greeting row:
  - Left: her square window with 'Vera · Tue 29 Sep'; the question at 44px with 'mind' stencilled; the ask well (3 rows, full width); From, mic and Send on one row; 'Send where I am'; the three ways to start on one row of plate keys.
  - Right: the Next up window with the radar (keep `.next-up`), and the vents and LED under it.
  - Then these rules: Finish setting up (amber lead and amber-ringed step numbers, no fill); Coming up with its slot and rows beside To do; Lately added beside the kids' wishes and Something to eat.
  - About 1700px or less at 1280.
- Ideas: the head row, then Search, the kind keys (latched: steel reverse #6b8396 with #0b0e0c words, a 2px #9cc4dc cap and a pinhole LED) and a For/Status disclosure beside the round window, then rows. At least 8 rows above the fold. The Kind select and the Restaurants tab are dropped: Restaurant is a key.
- Plans: the slot above the month. The month is printed on the plate: engraved grid, weekends shaded at a 60% slate mix, today in steel reverse with a pinhole. It fits one screen.
- To do: the slot, then Open/Done/Cancelled/All keys and Search, then rows with amber 'was due …' words and amber-ringed wells, and 'Edit or snooze' in words.
- Status: the 4:3 spend window at the head's right, with the figure also in words in the lede. The sections are rows with pinhole lamps, capped at 62rem.
- Chat:
  - The thread is on the plate.

## Round 13

Top four by score: r13-idea-1 Desk Terminal, Joined 8.33; r12-idea-2 Desk Terminal 7.85; r13-idea-2 Backlit Plate 7.8; r13-mut-2 Desk Terminal, Mapped 7.78.

- WHY WINNERS WON. Joined differed from its parent by 18-43% of pixels on every page (skeptic), and all of that change was for the better: a head row (title, then the one green primary) on every inner page, the Home box moved into the tube's last rows under the typed question, the terminal folded to a Ready line where nothing is live, month names in bone instead of fake-link denim, a lit NOW tick on To do, a moving-coil spend needle on Status, and 0 small targets on 13 pages. It was in seven top fours. This refines round 12's principle (a). Joined's open faults: a 290-700px dead void under the terminal on Home (make it sticky, or put the Contents plate back); the 40px VT323 tall-tick apostrophe in "What's" (third round running: use a straight glyph or set the question at the cell size); ways-to-start chips that touch (use an 8px gap); Vera shown three times on Chat; and on the phone Chat opens on the terminal, so the thread starts below the first screen (put the thread first).
- MUTANTS NEED PAGE-SCALE CHANGE. The phosphor mutant Track Diagram Aglow (7.06) was 0.1-0.9% different from its parent, and every lens but the feedback lens (which ranked it first, 8.9) called it a near-duplicate. Mapped changed only its tubes (0.2% on Chat, To do and Settings), yet still came 4th, because its two changes carried meaning. Lesson: a relight or restyle confined to lit things does not register. A mutation must change a structure the family reads, or add a device with a job. Aglow's one real fix, moving the setup tray from olive-bronze to slate, should spread; it closes the olive-tray issue from earlier rounds.
- TRAITS. seeds.json was empty for the third round, so again there is no evidence for the random slot. Informed entrants took 1st and 3rd. Graphics mutant (Mapped, 7.78, 3 promise votes): rewarded were the four one-meaning signals with a shape legend (on = lit lamp, waiting = steel dot, off = pewter ring, needs a look = amber bar, red only when something has stopped). Every lens wants this grafted, and it ends the red "no key" rings that read as alarms. Also rewarded: the Ideas map, with home lit at the centre and numbered dots at their true bearing and drive time. Not rewarded: the map's colliding 16px VT323 labels ("6 8 10" stacked, three downtown places on one dot), dots that are not links, aria-hidden, and replacing Home's radar sweep with an hours-of-day chart that reads as a spreadsheet. Keep the radar on Home and put the map on Ideas. Type mutant (Track Diagram, Monospaced, 6.32, 0 promise votes): Plex Mono 600 on row names, help and forms read as a code editor, wrapped labels and shrank controls to 12.8px. This confirms that mono is for figures, times and dates in fixed columns only. Crossover (Quote Board at Evening, 7.76, 5 top fours, 4 promise votes): Single Quote's head device on Evening Listing's slate took 53 small targets to 0. It had the fastest glance of the round, and the only row afterglow that registered in the capture. It was held back by costume (numbered bar keys 1-9, a '0' gear and an Alt-shortcut footer), filters hidden in folds, a yellow To do "4" beside amber "was due", and Vera's last reply set at headline size on Chat.
- FACES, SCALES AND PICTURES. Rewarded: Quote Board's condensed title, then the page figure in its section colour, then a stacked mono unit-and-change line. The type, system and interaction lenses all named it as the standard page head. Also rewarded: Backlit Plate's condensed 40px question with a true curly apostrophe; rule heads that carry a figure and a link at the right ("5 plans · All plans"); stacked "THU / 1" day columns; and a notes measure of 60-65ch. Folio's Fraunces figure-setting (fractions, a superscript $, the raised h in "2h10", calendar leaves) was admired, if used only for figures. Not rewarded: 96px thin folios ("990", "900", costume); whole phrases in letterspaced mono (Joined's "was due 2 days ago"); every row title underlined (Backlit Plate: underline at hover and focus only); leaders running 600px to the far edge (cap them at about 46rem); a 110px lowercase Outfit poster title (Dessau: cut it to 56-64px); and tracked or extended caps on nav and buttons (Blueprint, Grid, Catalogue, Folio, the switchboards). All four entrants that set the nav in caps or icons lost comprehension.
- FAILED REACHES. Backlit Plate (7.8, 5 promise votes, the most) has the clearest law for scarce light: light shows only through a cut in a matte plate, and the cut's shape says what it shows (a slot for time, a round window for place, 4:3 for the screen). On screen it read as plain: "mind" barely blooms, Status is one bare column, Settings and Family are only restyled, the 4:3 windows have spare glass, and one long slate sheet has no seams. Try again with engraved seams between bands, Add in the head, a round Next up radar window on Home, and the plate grammar carried to every page. Dessau Phosphor (6.47, 4 promise votes; the style lens ranked it first at 8.2): a round phosphor tube holding each page's one live figure, four shapes with four jobs and a legend in the footer, and a huge scanlined glowing "mind". It failed on a matte Bauhaus poster below the fold, navy cards (hue 259), ochre, terracotta and pink, 31 small targets, and To do reverting to cards with ISO dates. Keep the round screen and the shape legend on graphite. Signal Catalogue (5.71): its scope pulse per plan and its LED countdown meters are lovely lit data, sunk by the walnut ground (neutral hue 73). Graft the meters onto slate and make the pulse less like an ECG. Grid Console (6.16): its light-trail spine with section-coloured nodes and the only visible afterglow are worth keeping, without the Tron floor, the extended caps or the outlined cells. Blueprint (6.16): keep the date column with dimension-line "IN 2 DAYS" marks and the 24px baseline grid, with the grid confined to the margins, and drop the violet revision clouds. Folio Switchboard (6.88): keep its figure-setting.
- COLOUR. These failed: walnut or brass grounds (hue 73); navy card surfaces (#13171e, hue 259); a teal grid laid over the whole ground; violet for family lines or a "12" (off-period); brown, plum and teal fills on Lately added cards (put the kind colour in the ring lamp only); and amber doing two jobs (as a section colour and as late). The cobalt corner wash on Desk Terminal, Track Diagram and Quote Board is still invisible as a feature: drop it. Wheat or bone should carry section figures, under a 2px section cap, so amber means late only. The bronze fill on Traced's setup row still reads as selected.
- OPEN PROBLEMS. Row afterglow on hover is invisible in stills for the fifth round. Give it a visible 10-14% steel wash with a sage edge fading over about 1s, or drop it. The greeting's lit pool from below was lost by Joined and Backlit Plate: let the terminal spill a 60-80px green pool onto the desk. Every leader keeps a thick pewter or graphite monitor case: thin it to a 2-3px bezel with a hairline lip. The spend needle rests at zero in stills: add a limit tick and a ghost peak. Home says "5 plans" over 4 rows: say "4 more after Next up".
- CANDIDATE PRINCIPLES. (a) Every page opens on one head row: the title, the page's figure (with a stacked unit and change line), and its one green primary action. (b) State is coded by shape as well as colour, one meaning per signal, with a legend wherever lamps mean something, and red is reserved for something that has stopped. (c) A lit window's shape says what it shows, and it draws that page's own data, with marks numbered to the rows they stand for.
